rounds.robotnik_take: $537M at $2.96B post — the largest mineral-exploration venture round on record, anchoring KoBold as the AI-native critical-minerals comp to traditional majors Freeport-McMoRan (FCX), Rio Tinto (RIO), and BHP (BHP). Durable + T. Rowe leading signals crossover capital is treating Mingomba copper discovery as a pre-IPO setup, not a venture science bet. The thesis turns on whether ML-driven exploration produces a step-change in copper hit-rates versus a generation of seismic-only majors — a binary geological catalyst, not a software one.
rounds.company_description: Uses machine-learning models to identify and develop deposits of copper, lithium, nickel, and cobalt globally. Flagship project is the Mingomba copper deposit in Zambia; the company exists at the intersection of AI-driven exploration software and traditional mining operations.

rounds.co_investors: Zhangjiang Hi-Tech, Zhangke Yaokun Fund, Prosperity7 Ventures, Junshan Capital
rounds.robotnik_take: Series E at $1.1B post puts Fourier into the Chinese humanoid unicorn cohort alongside Unitree, Galbot, and Agibot — but valuation lags Spirit AI's $1.4B post-Series-A by an order of magnitude in funding efficiency. GR-2 platform competes with Tesla (TSLA) Optimus and Apptronik Apollo on the bipedal stack while rehab-robotics revenue gives Fourier near-term cashflow most peers lack. Guoxin/Pudong lead reads as state-municipal alignment; the bet is rehab-revenue funds the humanoid roadmap.
rounds.company_description: Chinese humanoid robot developer behind the GR-2 platform. Also operates a rehabilitation robotics business line for clinical use.

rounds.co_investors: Tiger Global Management, ArcTern Ventures, THOR Industries, Coca-Cola System Sustainability Fund, Ridgeline, Maniv Mobility, Ironspring, Schematic
rounds.robotnik_take: $100M Series B against a 4,690-unit / ~$500M order book — backlog-to-funding ratio is the cleanest in the EV-chassis class, contrasting with Canoo's collapse and Rivian (RIVN) / Workhorse (WKHS) burn rates. Tiger Global + Capricorn co-leading alongside THOR (THO) and Coca-Cola system signals strategic-anchor customer validation, not pure venture optionality. Medium-duty is the segment Ford (F) and Stellantis (STLA) under-serve; Harbinger's binary catalyst is converting the order book into delivered units without the chassis-startup death-by-NRE pattern.
rounds.company_description: Builds medium-duty electric truck chassis from a clean-sheet design for delivery, work-truck, and motorhome applications. Order book of approximately 4,690 vehicles worth around $500M; founded by alumni of Canoo and QuantumScape.

rounds.co_investors: BlueCrest Capital, Volvo Cars Tech Fund, InterAlpen Partners, Vsquared Ventures, HV Capital, Delta Electronics, C4 Ventures, L-Bank
rounds.robotnik_take: At the time, Europe's largest humanoid round — NEURA is the European counterweight to Apptronik, Figure, and 1X, with Volvo Cars Tech Fund anchoring auto-industry pull-through. Lingotto (Agnelli family) lead reads as Stellantis (STLA) / Ferrari (RACE) strategic positioning, not pure financial. 4NE1 third-gen targets the same warehouse / light-manufacturing TAM as Apollo and Optimus (TSLA), but with German industrial customers as the LTM revenue base. The bet is whether European OEMs procure domestically before US-trained models cross over.
rounds.company_description: Develops humanoid and cognitive robots equipped with onboard AI software for industrial and service applications. Flagship product is the 4NE1 humanoid, a 5.9-foot bipedal robot designed to understand natural-language instructions and handle payloads up to 220 pounds.

rounds.lead_investors: Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Glade Brook Capital
rounds.co_investors: Point72 Ventures, Woven Capital, 776, Industrious Ventures, Leitmotif, Y Combinator
rounds.robotnik_take: $260M Series C funds Nova rocket development and Cape Canaveral pad LC-14, the first US fully-reusable two-stage program after SpaceX. Comp set: Rocket Lab (RKLB) on partial reusability, Relativity and Blue Origin privately. The Breakthrough Energy + Glade Brook lead is a climate-aligned strategic syndicate signalling launch-decarbonization thesis. First Nova flight test is the binary milestone; subsequent Oct-25 Series D + Feb-26 extension validate investor conviction.
rounds.company_description: Develops Nova, a fully reusable two-stage medium-lift rocket. Both stages are designed to return and land for refurbishment. Targets US national security launch contracts (NSSL Phase 3 Lane 1) alongside commercial customers.

rounds.co_investors: Bpifrance, Foundation Capital, Temasek, Uncork Capital, Starburst VC, Supernova, Tribeca VP
rounds.robotnik_take: Unicorn round on $500M+ backlog — Loft is the hosted-payload comp to Planet (PL) and BlackSky (BKSY) on the recurring-bookings model, but differentiated by selling capacity rather than imagery. Tikehau + Temasek leading reads as sovereign infrastructure capital, not growth equity; Bpifrance participation flags French strategic alignment. The thesis: as launch cost collapses via SpaceX, satellite-as-a-service becomes the dominant procurement model for governments unwilling to operate their own birds. Execution risk is bus-supplier dependency, not demand.
rounds.company_description: Operates a 'space infrastructure as a service' business — builds and operates satellites carrying hosted payloads for customers who buy capacity rather than buying their own spacecraft. Backlog exceeds $500M across commercial and government customers.

rounds.co_investors: Battery Ventures, Partech, NGP Capital, Bpifrance Digital Venture, LFX, Shift4Good, Yamaha Motor Ventures
rounds.robotnik_take: $30M undisclosed tranche brings Shippeo total above $140M — competes directly with project44 and FourKites in real-time visibility, against the public-market read-through of Descartes (DSGX) and SPS Commerce (SPSC) on the supply-chain SaaS stack. Woven (Toyota) lead plus Yamaha Motor Ventures suggests Japanese OEM pull-through. APAC customer growth of 53% YoY is the only metric that differentiates Shippeo from project44; if APAC consolidation continues, Shippeo is the natural acquisition target for a logistics platform play.
rounds.company_description: Real-time multimodal transport visibility platform — software that tracks freight across road, rail, ocean, and air. Sells to shippers and carriers for supply-chain visibility; competes with project44 and FourKites.

rounds.co_investors: Andrew Forrest, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Eric Schmidt, John Doerr, Ken Griffin, Lachy Groom, Leitmotif, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Lowercarbon Capital, Mustafa Suleyman, Patrick Collison, Reid Hoffman, Richard Merkin, Trousdale Ventures
rounds.robotnik_take: Largest Series A in fusion history; pulsed magnetic approach with milestone-based tranches. Led by Hemant Taneja (General Catalyst). Investors: Andrew Forrest, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Eric Schmidt, John Doerr, Ken Griffin, Reid Hoffman, Mustafa Suleyman, Patrick Collison, Lightspeed, Lowercarbon Capital. Stealth-emerged Oct 2024.
rounds.company_description: Develops fusion energy using pulsed magnetic compression, a single-shot approach distinct from steady-state tokamak or laser inertial designs. Stealth-emerged in October 2024; commercialization milestones tied to tranched funding releases.

rounds.robotnik_take: $18M Series A on undisclosed lead — DLE category competes against Albemarle (ALB), SQM (SQM), and Standard Lithium (SLI) on the brine-extraction stack. Membrane-based separation is the differentiator versus solvent extraction; the thesis is unit economics at scale, not technology novelty. Sub-$25M tail round for the segment — the binary catalyst is a single commercial DLE plant demonstrating cost-down versus conventional brine evaporation.
rounds.company_description: Develops direct lithium extraction (DLE) technology using membrane-based separation for sustainable battery materials supply.

rounds.co_investors: Northern Powerhouse Investment Fund II, Praetura Ventures
rounds.robotnik_take: $5M seed for a cross-platform robotics SDK — competing with ROS-derived stacks and Viam's horizontal platform on the developer-infrastructure layer. Northern Gritstone lead is UK regional-deeptech capital, not venture-velocity. Comp set thin at this stage but adjacent reads: NVIDIA (NVDA) Isaac, ABB (ABB) RobotStudio on incumbent toolchains. Binary: developer adoption before larger horizontal players capture the SDK layer.
rounds.company_description: University of Sheffield spinout building a universal robotics software platform — an SDK enabling cross-platform robot programming across different hardware vendors.

rounds.robotnik_take: $425M Series F lifts Helion past $1B cumulative at $5.4B — pricing roughly parallel to Commonwealth Fusion ($6B at last raise) and well above TAE Technologies and Marvel Fusion on the inertial-confinement comp side. Microsoft (MSFT) 50MW PPA by 2028 is the only enforceable demand-side commitment in private fusion; that contract is also the binary catalyst — Helion either hits commercial first plasma against the PPA timeline or the valuation resets. Lightspeed + SoftBank lead reads as growth-capital signaling, not first-of-a-kind risk underwriting.
rounds.company_description: Develops a pulsed magneto-inertial fusion approach using helium-3 and deuterium, with direct electricity generation from plasma rather than steam turbines. Holds a power purchase agreement with Microsoft for a 50 MW plant targeted for 2028.

rounds.co_investors: Andreessen Horowitz, Lavrock Ventures, Cantos, First In, BlueYard Capital, Interlagos
rounds.robotnik_take: $70M equity + $30M debt Series A — ex-SpaceX team applying high-rate vertical integration to hypersonic strike weapons. Direct comp set: Lockheed Martin (LMT) and Raytheon (RTX) on the incumbent missile primes, Anduril and Stoke Space on the new-defense-prime model. Lightspeed leading with a16z, BlueYard, Cantos signals the Anduril-template playbook is being copied. The thesis: DoD pricing per hypersonic round will collapse if Castelion's SpaceX-style manufacturing transfers to munitions — a binary on cost-per-unit, not technology.
rounds.company_description: Builds the Blackbeard hypersonic strike weapon for the US Army and Navy. Founded by former SpaceX engineers applying high-rate, vertically integrated manufacturing methods to hypersonic missile production.

rounds.robotnik_take: $52M Series B for Japan's leading micro-satellite integrator — comp set: Mitsubishi Electric (6503 JP) and IHI (7013 JP) on the incumbent Japanese aerospace side, plus Rocket Lab (RKLB) on the vertically integrated smallsat-bus model. Incubate Fund lead reads as Japan-domestic capital depth, not international growth signal. Thesis: Japan's MoD smallsat procurement is reshoring from US suppliers; ArkEdge is the most plausible domestic prime. Binary catalyst is the next JAXA / MoD constellation contract.
rounds.company_description: Japanese satellite system integrator scaling micro-satellite production for commercial and government constellations. Operates as a vertically integrated supplier of buses, payloads, and mission management.

rounds.lead_investors: Google, SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Valor Equity Partners
rounds.co_investors: QVT Family Office, Safar Partners
rounds.robotnik_take: $230M convertible note led by Google (GOOG), SoftBank Vision Fund 2, and Valor — the cap-stack signal is that QuEra is being positioned as the neutral-atom leader against IonQ (IONQ), Rigetti (RGTI), and D-Wave (QBTS) on the public-market side, plus PsiQuantum and Quantinuum privately. $41M Japan supercomputing-center sale is the only real commercial-revenue datapoint in modal neutral-atom. Convertible structure rather than equity reads as price-discovery deferral by Google — they want the option without setting the mark. Modality bet, not company bet.
rounds.company_description: Builds neutral-atom quantum computers using arrays of optically trapped rubidium atoms as qubits. Spun out of Harvard and MIT research; customers include Japanese supercomputing centers.

rounds.co_investors: Google/DeepMind
rounds.robotnik_take: $350M Series A at $1.5B post (later expanded to $403M) — Apptronik is now the Western pure-play humanoid comp to Figure, 1X, and Agility on the bipedal-warehouse stack, against Tesla (TSLA) Optimus on the integrated-OEM side. Google/DeepMind co-investing is the structural differentiator: Apollo gets a foundation-model partner most peers lack. Mercedes-Benz pilot is the early procurement signal. Binary catalyst is converting the Mercedes pilot into a multi-thousand-unit contract before US capital tightens on humanoid burn rates.
rounds.company_description: Builds Apollo, a general-purpose humanoid robot for warehouse and manufacturing work. Partnered with Mercedes-Benz for factory pilot deployments; targets logistics and automotive industrial customers.

rounds.co_investors: Samsung Ventures, In-Q-Tel, RTX Ventures, HH-CTBC (Foxconn/CTBC), Maverick Silicon
rounds.robotnik_take: $100M Series B for analog in-memory inference — comp set: NVIDIA (NVDA) on digital-incumbent, TSMC (TSM) as the fab partner, plus Mythic (private) and Syntiant on the analog-AI thesis. Tiger Global lead reads as growth-stage signaling, while Samsung Ventures + RTX Ventures + In-Q-Tel give defense and Korean memory pull-through. Energy-per-inference is the only credible angle versus GPU incumbents at the edge. Binary: a single tier-1 client SoC design-win demonstrating production-grade yield on TSMC nodes — analog-CMOS yield is the cliff that killed the prior generation.
rounds.company_description: Designs analog in-memory compute AI inference chips, targeting energy-efficient inference for edge and client devices. Differentiated from digital accelerators by reducing the data-movement penalty that constrains GPU power efficiency.

rounds.co_investors: Alpine Space Ventures, First Round Capital
rounds.robotnik_take: $110M Series B for Mega-class high-power buses — K2 is the post-Starship bet: bus capability designed around the launch-cost collapse SpaceX has now demonstrated. Comp set: Lockheed Martin (LMT) and Maxar (private) on the incumbent large-bus side; Rocket Lab (RKLB) and Loft Orbital on the new-entrant smallsat side. Lightspeed + Altimeter leading reads as growth-stage validation that the heavy-lift thesis is real. Binary catalyst is the first Mega-class delivery to a defense or constellation customer before competitors retool to match the payload class.
rounds.company_description: Develops Mega-class high-power satellites — large, high-capability spacecraft designed for the heavy-lift launch era opened by Starship-class vehicles. Sells to constellation operators and government customers wanting more capability per spacecraft than current smallsat designs.

rounds.co_investors: British Patient Capital, Parkwalk, BGF, Cambridge Innovation Capital, Foresight Group, IQ Capital
rounds.robotnik_take: $32M Series C against GaN power incumbents: Infineon (IFX DE), Navitas (NVTS), Wolfspeed (WOLF), and EPC (private) — Cambridge GaN is the smallest player in the public-market comp set by an order of magnitude. Strategic-investor lead with British Patient Capital signals UK domestic-semis support, not aggressive growth thesis. Data-center 48V conversion is the only segment where Cambridge GaN can credibly compete on volume; binary is a single hyperscaler design-win before Infineon's monolithic GaN ICs reach production scale.
rounds.company_description: UK Cambridge University spinout designing gallium nitride (GaN) power transistors and ICs for industrial, data center, and automotive applications. Competes with Infineon, EPC, and Navitas in GaN power semiconductors.

rounds.co_investors: Bullnet Capital, EIC Fund, Intel Capital, MONDRAGON Corporation, TEL Venture Capital
rounds.robotnik_take: $10.5M Series C for wavefront-phase metrology — competing against KLA (KLAC) and Applied Materials (AMAT) on the wafer-inspection stack, plus Onto Innovation (ONTO) and Camtek (CAMT) on the smaller-cap end. Samsung Ventures + Intel Capital + TEL Venture lead is the unusual signal: three of the largest fab and equipment customers are funding the same metrology supplier. Phemet tool's lateral resolution at advanced nodes is the binary. Sub-$25M round; deal economics priced for foothold, not category leadership.
rounds.company_description: Spanish developer of wavefront-phase imaging metrology tools for advanced-node semiconductor wafers, an alternative to traditional interferometry. Intel Capital is a strategic investor; launching the Phemet fab metrology tool from a new Tenerife cleanroom.

rounds.co_investors: General Catalyst, Andreessen Horowitz, 8VC, Caffeinated Capital, NightDragon, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Point72 Ventures
rounds.robotnik_take: Port Alpha is the load-bearing piece — first new US Navy-grade greenfield shipyard in decades positions Saronic as the domestic shipbuilding picks-and-shovels play, not just an ASV vendor. Comp set: Huntington Ingalls (HII) and Austal (ASB AU) on hulls, Leidos (LDOS) and L3Harris (LHX) on integration, HavocAI and Anduril Marine private-side. $4B post is 4x prior round — pricing the unmanned-fleet thesis ahead of Replicator volume contracts and CHIPS-of-the-sea capacity build.
rounds.company_description: Builds autonomous surface vessels (Spyglass, Cutlass, Corsair classes) for the US Navy and allied maritime forces. Founded by a former Navy SEAL; building Port Alpha, a dedicated autonomous shipyard for mass production of unmanned vessels.

rounds.co_investors: NVentures (NVIDIA), ARK Invest, In-Q-Tel, Andrej Karpathy, Pegatron, Supermicro, Wistron, G Squared
rounds.robotnik_take: $480M Series D at multi-billion valuation funds Blackwell B200 buildout; 25,000+ GPU fleet positions Lambda as the merchant alternative to CoreWeave (CRWV) and hyperscaler AI clouds. Comp set: CoreWeave on listed GPU cloud, Crusoe and Together AI on private peers, Oracle (ORCL) on hyperscaler GPU rental. Capital intensity is the binary question — Lambda's lifetime raise sits a tier below CoreWeave's debt-heavy capital stack.
rounds.company_description: Operates an AI cloud service that rents NVIDIA GPU servers for AI training and inference. Manages over 25,000 GPUs across its data centers, adding Blackwell B200s in 2025; competes with CoreWeave and the hyperscaler clouds.

rounds.co_investors: Voima Ventures, Lunar Ventures, Dhyan Ventures, Tiny Supercomputer VC, Atomico Angel
rounds.robotnik_take: EUR 15M equity + EUR 2.5M grants Series A — cryo-CMOS targets the qubit-control-electronics layer that has to scale with qubit counts. Comp set: Intel (INTC) Horse Ridge II on the in-house cryo-CMOS side, plus Quantum Machines and Zurich Instruments on the room-temp control side. EIC Accelerator lead is grant capital, not growth signaling. VTT pedigree gives Finnish national-lab fab access. Binary: integration with a major qubit vendor (IBM, Google, IonQ) before in-house cryo-CMOS solutions productize.
rounds.company_description: Finnish VTT spinout designing cryo-CMOS chips for control electronics in quantum computers. Targets the control-electronics layer that scales alongside qubit counts in superconducting and spin-qubit quantum systems.

rounds.co_investors: Maverick Capital, Fundomo, EPIQ Capital Group, Jim Keller (Tenstorrent CEO)
rounds.robotnik_take: $21.5M seed for RISC-V high-performance application processors — comp set: SiFive and Tenstorrent (Jim Keller) on the RISC-V architecture side, against Intel (INTC), AMD (AMD), and ARM (ARM) on the licensed/integrated incumbents. Eclipse Ventures lead plus Keller as angel signals architect-network capital, not platform-velocity yet. Ex-Intel CPU team is the thesis: per-core performance leadership in RISC-V has been the white-whale of the ecosystem. Binary catalyst is a tape-out demonstrating credible IPC against ARM v9.
rounds.company_description: Develops high-performance RISC-V application processors for AI, cloud, and edge compute, founded by former Intel CPU architects. Targets per-core performance leadership in the RISC-V ecosystem.

rounds.robotnik_take: $102M Series B for Chinese domestic photomask supply — direct comp set: Photronics (PLAB) and Toppan (7911 JP) on the global photomask incumbents, against domestic substitution targets like SMIC (981 HK) and Hua Hong (1347 HK) on demand-side. Investor list undisclosed but round size signals state-aligned capital depth. Photomasks are an under-appreciated chokepoint in China's semiconductor self-sufficiency push — the binary is whether Puzhao can serve advanced-node masks before US export controls tighten further.
rounds.company_description: Chinese manufacturer of photomasks used in IC lithography. Part of China's domestic chip supply push to reduce dependence on Photronics and Japanese photomask suppliers.

rounds.co_investors: Intel Capital, Red Dot Capital Partners
rounds.robotnik_take: $170M Series C at $700M post — Quantum Machines is the Switzerland of quantum: serves more than half of active quantum companies regardless of modality. Comp set: IonQ (IONQ), Rigetti (RGTI), and D-Wave (QBTS) on the public modality side; Keysight (KEYS) as the test-and-measurement analog. PSG Equity lead plus Intel Capital co-invest signals growth and strategic alignment. Thesis: control-electronics revenue scales with industry-wide qubit count, not modality winners. Picks-and-shovels at fair price.
rounds.company_description: Provides quantum control hardware and software — the OPX+ controller and QUA programming language — that orchestrate qubit operations. Customers include more than half of the active quantum computing companies worldwide, regardless of qubit modality.

rounds.robotnik_take: HTS tokamak design; compact spherical tokamak advancing; DOE Milestone Program.
rounds.company_description: Develops a compact spherical tokamak fusion reactor using high-temperature superconducting (HTS) magnets. UK-based; participates in the US DOE Milestone-Based Fusion Development Program and also commercializes HTS magnet technology.

rounds.co_investors: Battery Ventures, Neurone
rounds.robotnik_take: $30M Series C — Viam is the horizontal robotics OS comp to Physical Intelligence on the model layer and ROS-derived stacks on the open-source layer, plus PTC's (PTC) ThingWorx on the industrial-IoT-software side. Eliot Horowitz's MongoDB-derived playbook reads as developer-infra-first, vertical-application-second. Union Square + Battery + Neurone is a small-check insider round, not a growth-stage signal. Binary: whether Viam captures meaningful share of the OEM SDK layer before NVIDIA (NVDA) Isaac and AWS RoboMaker compress the developer-tooling pricing power.
rounds.company_description: Provides a horizontal software platform — a robotics and IoT operating system — for connecting and managing smart machines. Founded by MongoDB co-founder Eliot Horowitz; positions as developer infrastructure rather than vertical robotics.

rounds.co_investors: General Dynamics Land Systems, StepStone Group, T. Rowe Price, NightDragon, Manhattan Venture Partners
rounds.robotnik_take: $250M Series D at $1.35B post-money positions Epirus as the best-capitalized pure-play HPM counter-drone vendor. Comp set: Anduril (private) on broader defense-tech, RTX (RTX) and Lockheed (LMT) on incumbent directed-energy, no public pure-play. Pentagon Leonidas IDIQ award is the binary catalyst. The 2x step-up from Series C signals continued defense-tech momentum through the autonomy procurement cycle.
rounds.company_description: Develops the Leonidas high-power microwave system for counter-drone and counter-electronics use. Sells solid-state directed-energy weapons to the US Army and allied militaries.

rounds.co_investors: Andreessen Horowitz, US Innovative Technology Fund, Washington Harbour Partners
rounds.robotnik_take: $240M Series F at $5.3B post — Shield AI is the autonomy-software comp to Anduril on the vertically integrated defense-prime side, plus AeroVironment (AVAV), Kratos (KTOS), and Northrop (NOC) on the public-market autonomy stack. L3Harris (LHX) + Hanwha Aerospace co-leading is the structural signal: incumbent primes are buying influence in the software layer rather than building. V-BAT plus Hivemind-equipped F-16 retrofits make Shield AI the rare both-platform-and-software bet. Binary catalyst is the first Hivemind program-of-record award at scale.
rounds.company_description: Develops Hivemind, an AI autonomy stack for military aircraft and drones that enables operation in GPS- and communications-denied environments. Products include the V-BAT vertical-takeoff UAV and Hivemind-equipped fighter jet retrofits.

rounds.robotnik_take: $115M is an outlier seed — Eclipse Ventures anchoring an RJ Scaringe-led Rivian spinout with proprietary auto-manufacturing data. Comp set: Symbotic (SYM) on warehouse automation, Rockwell (ROK) on industrial automation, plus private peers Apptronik and Figure AI on the humanoid side. The Rivian-data-flywheel pitch is unique in the seed cohort — closest analog is Tesla's Optimus internal program. Four months later the Series A priced at $2B valuation with Accel and a16z, validating the seed thesis but pricing in the entire data-advantage moat upfront.
rounds.company_description: Mind Robotics is a Rivian spinout building AI-enabled robotic systems for complex manufacturing tasks requiring dexterity, adaptability, and real-time decision-making, leveraging Rivian operations data as a foundation. Led by Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe.

rounds.robotnik_take: $150M Series G — Distalmotion is the mobile-cost-disruption bet against Intuitive Surgical (ISRG) da Vinci, with Asensus Surgical (ASXC) and CMR Surgical on adjacent challenger cohort. Dexter targets ambulatory surgery centers — a segment ISRG's footprint and price point don't fit. Revival Healthcare Capital lead reads as concentrated late-stage healthcare-tech capital. Three FDA clearances (gallbladder, hysterectomy, hernia) is the commercial unlock. Binary: ASC adoption scaling procedure volume before ISRG counters with a smaller-footprint platform.
rounds.company_description: Builds Dexter, a smaller, mobile surgical robot for ambulatory surgery centers, designed to compete with Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci on cost and footprint. FDA-cleared for gallbladder removal, hysterectomy, and hernia repair.

rounds.co_investors: BlackRock, Tiger Global Management, Maverick Silicon, Lip-Bu Tan, AMD Ventures, Koch Disruptive, Temasek, Xora, Porsche SE, The Engine Ventures
rounds.robotnik_take: $250M Series C funds Photonic Fabric optical interconnect for AI memory-disaggregation; positions Celestial alongside Lightmatter and Ayar Labs as the merchant alternatives to in-house hyperscaler photonics. Comp set: Lightmatter ($4.4B), Ayar Labs (Intel-aligned), Marvell (MRVL) and Broadcom (AVGO) on CPO. AMD strategic LP is the load-bearing signal — accelerator incumbent hedging into optical I/O before HBM/copper power walls bind.
rounds.company_description: Develops the Photonic Fabric optical interconnect — silicon photonic chiplets that disaggregate memory from compute for AI clusters at higher bandwidth than electrical NVLink or Tomahawk-class switching. Targets hyperscalers building exascale AI systems.

rounds.robotnik_take: $15M Series A — DALP positioned as the additive-deposition counterpart to ASM International (ASM NA) and Lam Research (LRCX) on incumbent ALD. STMicro (STM) and Sony (6758 JP) partnerships are the differentiator — these are tool-validation revenue, not pilot-conversion. NASA / ESA deployments are flagship references but small revenue. Sub-$25M round priced for tool-platform proof, not category leadership. Binary catalyst is a production-grade chamber qualified at a tier-1 logic fab.
rounds.company_description: Danish developer of Direct Atomic Layer Processing (DALP) equipment for semiconductor, quantum device, and optics manufacturing. Tools deployed at NASA and ESA; partners include STMicroelectronics and Sony.

rounds.co_investors: March Capital, ARK Venture Fund, Altitude Life Science Ventures, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority
rounds.robotnik_take: $200M seed is among the largest ever — Lila is Flagship Pioneering's biotech-platform playbook applied to AI + lab automation. Comp set: Recursion (RXRX) and Insitro (private) on the AI-for-drug-discovery side, Schrodinger (SDGR) on the in-silico stack, against Bruker (BRKR) and Thermo Fisher (TMO) on the lab-automation hardware. Flagship + General Catalyst lead reads as institutional conviction stacking, not seed-stage capital. The thesis: closed-loop AI plus lab robots produces faster materials/chem discovery than either alone. Series A bar is now extreme.
rounds.company_description: Builds an AI-driven scientific discovery platform combining foundation models with automated laboratory experimentation for materials, chemistry, and biology research. Targets pharma and industrial R&D customers wanting closed-loop AI + lab automation.

rounds.robotnik_take: $55M extension — Marvel is the laser-driven-fusion comp to NIF on the inertial-confinement physics path, against Helion (magneto-inertial) and Commonwealth (tokamak) on the broader fusion-investment frame. EQT Ventures + Siemens Energy lead is the structural signal: Siemens Energy (ENR DE) gives Marvel a downstream grid-integration partner most fusion peers lack. Colorado State $150M facility is the research-to-commercial pathway. Binary catalyst is laser-target ignition demonstration on a non-NIF platform.
rounds.company_description: German laser-driven inertial confinement fusion company. Building a fusion research facility with Colorado State University to validate the laser-target approach in a research-to-commercial pathway.

rounds.co_investors: SoftBank, Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, DCVC, Playground Global, NVentures (NVIDIA), Sony Innovation Fund, Schaeffler, TDK Ventures, Safar Partners
rounds.robotnik_take: $400M Series C at $2.12B post — Digit is in active Amazon (AMZN) warehouse deployment, giving Agility the only confirmed multi-thousand-unit demand-side commitment in Western humanoid. Comp set: Figure, Apptronik, and 1X privately; Tesla (TSLA) Optimus on the OEM-integrated side. WP Global lead with SoftBank, Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, and NVentures (NVDA) co-investing reads as strategic-customer stack and supply-chain alignment. RoboFab 10K/yr target is the operational binary: hit the run-rate or the valuation resets versus humanoid peers still pre-production.
rounds.company_description: Builds Digit, a bipedal humanoid robot designed for warehouse and logistics work. Operates RoboFab in Salem, Oregon — a manufacturing facility targeting 10,000 robots per year — and deploys Digit in Amazon warehouses.

rounds.co_investors: All existing major investors
rounds.robotnik_take: $200M tranche funds US FDA submission and commercial buildout for Versius soft-tissue platform. Comp set: ISRG (Intuitive) dominant incumbent, Medtronic Hugo and Stryker Mako on adjacent platforms, Asensus (ASXC) on listed peers. CMR is the best-capitalized private soft-tissue RAS challenger globally; US 510(k) clearance is the binary catalyst that unlocks the world's largest surgical robotics market and the path to a strategic exit or IPO.
rounds.company_description: Develops the Versius surgical robotic system for soft-tissue laparoscopic surgery. The platform is modular — separate arms on independent carts instead of a single bulky tower — and competes with Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci across more than 15,000 procedures globally.

rounds.robotnik_take: $50M Series A for space-based solar — orbital arrays plus laser/microwave downlink. Comp set thin: no listed pure-play comp; adjacencies are Northrop (NOC) on space-power systems and First Solar (FSLR) on terrestrial PV. Index + Interlagos lead is venture-conviction capital. Defense and remote-power use cases are the only credible early markets — grid-scale economics remain speculative. Binary: production ramp and automotive/IoT design-wins converting before edge-AI digital MAC roadmaps eliminate the analog efficiency edge.
rounds.company_description: Designs analog in-memory compute AI inference chips that perform matrix multiplications directly in flash-memory cells rather than digital MAC units. Targets edge AI workloads in industrial, IoT, and automotive applications.

rounds.co_investors: Andreessen Horowitz, ARK Invest, DCVC, Founders Fund, Align Ventures, Chevron Tech Ventures
rounds.robotnik_take: $300M Series D — Radiant is the portable-microreactor bet (1MW HTGR Kaleidos) for DoD forward-base diesel-generator displacement, against BWX Technologies (BWXT), X-energy, and Oklo (OKLO) on the SMR/microreactor cohort. Draper + Boost VC lead with a16z, ARK, Founders Fund, and Chevron Tech Ventures reads as deep-tech-plus-energy crossover capital. Defense-distributed-energy urgency drives the round size. Binary: NRC licensing milestones plus a first DoD-deployed unit before incumbents move portable-class hardware through certification.
rounds.company_description: Develops portable nuclear microreactors — semi-truck-sized 1 MW high-temperature gas reactors (Kaleidos) for remote installations and defense forward bases. Targets the diesel generator replacement market for the US Department of Defense.

rounds.co_investors: SVB, Pinegrove Venture Partners, Hercules Capital
rounds.robotnik_take: $150M Series E — HawkEye 360 is the RF-SIGINT satellite-constellation bet for maritime, defense, and intelligence customers, against Spire Global (SPIR) and Kleos Space (private) on the RF cohort, plus BlackSky (BKSY) and Planet (PL) on broader EO reference. Dark-vessel and jamming detection is the structural complement to optical/SAR data. NightDragon + Center15 Capital lead with SVB and Hercules debt reads as cyber-defense-plus-venture-debt capital. Binary: NRO contract renewals and new constellation deployments before SPIR-class players extend RF SIGINT natively.
rounds.company_description: Operates a constellation of RF signal-intelligence satellites that geolocate radio emitters for maritime, defense, and intelligence customers. Detects dark vessels, jamming, and other RF activity invisible to optical or SAR sensors.

rounds.robotnik_take: $1.1B IPO on Shanghai STAR Market — Moore Threads is the Chinese GPU-self-sufficiency listing against NVIDIA (NVDA) and AMD (AMD) on the global GPU tape, with Cambricon (688256 CH) and Biren (private) on domestic Chinese AI-silicon cohort. US export controls confine the addressable market to domestic Chinese customers. STAR Market float reads as state-aligned capital-market support for AI-self-sufficiency policy. Binary: next-gen GPU tape-out and Chinese-government procurement volumes validating the policy-anchored revenue base.
rounds.company_description: Chinese designer of general-purpose GPUs for AI and graphics applications. Public on Shanghai STAR Market; competes with NVIDIA and AMD in the GPU market, though primarily serves domestic Chinese customers due to US export controls.

rounds.co_investors: Y Combinator, Pegasus Tech Ventures, Protocol Labs, Halo Labs, Asymmetry Ventures, TRAC VC
rounds.robotnik_take: $15M seed — Enlightra is the chip-scale multiwavelength laser bet replacing copper with optical interconnects at AI-data-center scale-up, against Coherent (COHR), Lumentum (LITE), and II-VI (now COHR) on the laser incumbents, plus Ayar Labs and Lightmatter on the silicon-photonics cohort. Runa Capital lead with Y Combinator and Protocol Labs reads as deeptech-plus-Web3-crossover seed capital. Nobel-contributing research provenance is the technical signal. Sub-$25M tail. Binary: 2027 pilot production execution before NVDA/MRVL/AVGO lock optical-interconnect supply.
rounds.company_description: Swiss-US developer of chip-scale multiwavelength lasers that replace copper wiring with optical interconnects for AI data center scale-up. Pilot production planned for 2027; founded by Nobel Prize-contributing researchers.

rounds.lead_investors: China Mobile Industry Chain Leader Fund
rounds.co_investors: CICC Capital, Chinese Academy of Sciences Fund, Suzhou Venture Capital, CMG Media Fund
rounds.robotnik_take: $300M Undisclosed at $3.0B post — Galbot is among the largest Chinese humanoid rounds, in cohort with Unitree, Agibot, X Square Robot, and Robot Era, with Tesla (TSLA) Optimus, XPeng (XPEV) Iron, and Figure on Western reference. China Mobile Industry Chain Leader Fund lead with CICC, Chinese Academy of Sciences Fund, and Suzhou VC reads as state-aligned-plus-academic-strategic capital. General-purpose embodied-AI is the platform pitch. Binary: mass-production timeline and enterprise pilot deployments versus Western cohort consolidation.
rounds.company_description: Chinese humanoid robot developer building general-purpose embodied AI platforms for industrial and service applications. Backed by China Mobile's Industry Chain Leader Fund; competes with Agibot, Unitree, and Tesla Optimus.

rounds.co_investors: Alibaba Group, Tencent Holdings, Wang Huiwen (Meituan co-founder)
rounds.robotnik_take: Notable for what's said — "rules out quick IPO" — more than the dollar amount. With Alibaba and Tencent both anchoring alongside IDG, Moonshot is now structurally a BABA-Tencent joint AI champion, not an independent. Comp set in Chinese LLMs: StepFun (state-backed), DeepSeek (privately funded), Zhipu, MiniMax, Baidu (BIDU) ERNIE. Kimi consumer pull is real; enterprise monetization vs API price compression is the open question. Less interesting as a fundraise, more as cap-table consolidation.
rounds.company_description: Chinese AI lab developing the Kimi large language model and consumer-facing chat assistant. One of China's leading LLM platforms alongside ByteDance Doubao, Baidu ERNIE, and Alibaba Qwen.

rounds.co_investors: MVP Ventures, additional undisclosed investors
rounds.robotnik_take: Lockheed Martin Ventures co-leading with 8VC is the load-bearing fact — LMV anchoring an AI/chemical-informatics platform signals defense supply chain is now sourcing materials discovery the way it sources software. Comp set: Citrine Informatics on materials-informatics pure-play, Phaseshift on alloy discovery, Aionics on battery materials, plus Schrödinger (SDGR) on the computational side; Albemarle (ALB) is the only public proxy for advanced-monomer manufacturing. Aerospace and defense are the highest-margin verticals, and LM's anchor essentially pre-commits offtake.
rounds.company_description: AI and chemical-informatics platform that designs advanced monomers and polymers for aerospace, defense, and high-performance industrial applications. Lockheed Martin Ventures is a strategic investor anchoring defense-supply-chain offtake.

rounds.co_investors: Exor Ventures, Key1 Capital, VentureTech Alliance, Willenz
rounds.robotnik_take: Ex-Apple Face ID team building cross-platform depth-sensing for AMRs, arms, robotaxis, and humanoids is the cleanest hire-the-team bet in robotics perception this cycle. Comp set: Mobileye (MBLY) on AV perception, Outsight on solid-state LiDAR, Aeva (AEVA) on FMCW, Luminar (LAZR) on automotive-grade; Nodar on stereo vision. Fidelity + Atreides leading with Exor strategic (Agnelli industrial holding) is an unusual cap table — Exor's presence hints at Stellantis or CNH Industrial OEM design-win path.
rounds.company_description: Develops the LyteVision depth-sensing perception platform for autonomous mobile robots, robotic arms, robotaxis, and humanoids. Founded by alumni of the Apple Face ID team; sells perception modules and software to robot OEMs.

rounds.co_investors: CJIC, M7 Holdings
rounds.robotnik_take: Singapore LFP-recycling pre-Series A with SGInnovate and Shift4Good is sovereign-aligned ASEAN capital — LFP-specific positioning matters because LFP recovery economics are still unproven vs. NMC cathode value. Comp set: Li-Cycle (post-restructuring) on US Spoke-and-Hub LFP, Redwood Materials and Ascend Elements as the US incumbents, Cirba Solutions on US recycling, Princeton NuEnergy on direct cathode recycling; CATL (300750 CH) as the LFP cell-maker offtake counterparty. Pilot-plant commissioning is the binary milestone.
rounds.company_description: Singapore-based battery materials recycling and upcycling startup focused on LFP cell recycling. Competes with Li-Cycle and Redwood Materials in battery recycling.

rounds.co_investors: FirstMark Capital, Financiere Saint James, Kima Ventures
rounds.robotnik_take: Dassault Aviation leading puts a French aerospace prime directly on the cap table of a defense-AI software unicorn — closest analog is Helsing's Saab integration and Anduril's Lattice positioning. Comp set: Helsing ($12B private), Anduril, Quantum Systems on the European defense-AI side. Strategic frame is Rafale and FCAS autonomy: Dassault gets a captive software layer, Harmattan gets guaranteed program integration. €1.4B is rich for Series B but in line with European defense-AI peers post-2022 EU spend reset.
rounds.company_description: French defense-tech company developing autonomy software and mission systems for combat aircraft and drones. Anchored by strategic backing from Dassault Aviation; positioned as France's defense-AI counterpart to Anduril and Helsing.

rounds.co_investors: NVentures (NVIDIA), Macquarie Capital, Bezos Expeditions, 1789 Capital, Disruptive, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Felicis Ventures, Coatue, Sequoia Capital, Samsung, LG, Schneider, CommonSpirit, Salesforce Ventures
rounds.robotnik_take: Largest pure robotics-software round ever and the clearest signal that capital is separating the robot-brain layer from the robot-body layer. Comp set on the brain side: Physical Intelligence (11B private), Rhoda AI (1.7B), Galaxea AI (2.9B in China). The strategic frame is OEM-agnostic licensing — a picks-and-shovels bet that the humanoid winners won't build their own foundation models. SoftBank-led syndicate alongside NVIDIA, Samsung, LG, Bezos is the most strategically loaded cap table in the cycle.
rounds.company_description: Develops a general-purpose robot foundation model — a single AI 'brain' designed to work across different robot bodies. Pittsburgh-based; targets robot OEMs and integrators that want to license the underlying control intelligence rather than build it in-house.

rounds.robotnik_take: Total raise approaching 1B for a pre-revenue ASIC bet on transformer architecture lock-in — the highest-conviction architectural wager in the dataset. Comp set: Groq (private, LPU on inference), Cerebras (wafer-scale), Tenstorrent on the alt-architecture side; NVIDIA (NVDA) as the architectural counter. If transformers stay dominant through 2027-28, Etched's Sohu economics are differentiated; if Mamba/SSM/diffusion architectures take meaningful share, the hardwiring becomes a liability. TSM (TSM) 4nm production timeline is the pacing constraint.
rounds.company_description: Designs the Sohu chip, a transformer-specific ASIC that hardwires the transformer architecture into silicon to outperform general-purpose GPUs on transformer inference. Manufactured at TSMC 4nm; targets inference workloads where transformer dominance makes specialization economical.

rounds.robotnik_take: Avenir Growth leading solo on a $120M Series C at ~$570M is unusually concentrated for ASRS — growth-stage warehouse-automation rounds typically syndicate 2-3 leads given the capital intensity. Comp set: Symbotic (SYM) as the public benchmark, AutoStore (AUTO NO) on the public side, Exotec and Geek+ as private peers. Ex-Tesla founder DNA is the differentiator, and climbing 3D-movement architecture is genuinely novel vs grid-shuttle approaches. Fortune-100 deployment is the catalyst; SYM's operational stumbles open the comp window.
rounds.company_description: Builds a software-defined warehouse automation platform using climbing robots that move heavy material in three dimensions. Founded by former Tesla engineers; competes with Symbotic, AutoStore, and Exotec in ASRS.

rounds.robotnik_take: Mitsubishi Electric leading at $1.3B unicorn signals Japanese industrial primes are buying their DX strategy rather than building it — the same pattern as Honda/Tulip and Toyota/Daido earlier in the cycle. Comp set: Siemens (SIE GR) MES, PTC (PTC) ThingWorx, Rockwell (ROK) FactoryTalk; AspenTech (now part of Emerson, EMR) on AI-enabled industrial software. No-code MES is consolidating around a small number of platforms, and Tulip's pharma/biotech traction gives it a vertical the legacy MES vendors are weaker in.
rounds.company_description: No-code frontline-operations platform for manufacturing and life sciences, with AI embedded in workflow apps for operators and quality teams. Sells to discrete manufacturers and pharma/biotech producers; Mitsubishi Electric is a strategic investor.

rounds.lead_investors: China Development Bank Capital, Guozhong Capital, CCTV Media Convergence Industry Investment Fund
rounds.co_investors: Xuhui Capital, Wuxi state-backed funds, Lanchi Venture Capital, Hillhouse
rounds.robotnik_take: Heavily state-backed syndicate (China Development Bank Capital + CCTV Media + Guozhong + Wuxi/Shanghai state funds) marks PsiBot as a designated national champion in dexterous manipulation — distinct from the strategic-corporate-led structure at Unitree or X Square (Xiaomi-anchored). Meituan partnership for last-mile logistics robot and NVIDIA (NVDA) sim-training collaboration are the commercial pull-throughs. Comp set: Galaxea (brain-layer), Unitree, Galbot on robotics; the dexterous-manipulation focus narrows the field meaningfully.
rounds.company_description: Chinese embodied-AI company developing dexterous-manipulation humanoid robots, including the PsiBot V1 wheeled dual-arm platform and the Psi-R series of vision-language-action models. Partnered with Meituan for the 'Little Yellow Bee' logistics robot and with NVIDIA on simulation training.

rounds.co_investors: Cornerstone Capital, Sichuan Zhenxing Group
rounds.robotnik_take: Guotai Junan Innovation Investment leading signals Chinese quantum is being treated as a state-priority sector under the 15th Five-Year Plan — the same financing pattern that mobilized capital into power-semis and EUV-adjacent equipment. Comp set: Origin Quantum, QuantumCTek (688027), QBoson on the domestic side; IBM (IBM), IonQ (IONQ), Rigetti (RGTI) on the US public side. 40-country deployment suggests the educational/scientific tier is being commoditized faster than expected. Superconducting-revenue shift is the technical update.
rounds.company_description: Chinese quantum computing company developing superconducting and NMR-based quantum systems for industrial and educational customers. Targets the domestic Chinese quantum hardware market under the 15th Five-Year Plan.

rounds.lead_investors: Fidelity Management & Research, Baillie Gifford, Valor Equity Partners, Tiger Global Management
rounds.co_investors: Fidelity Management & Research, Baillie Gifford, Tiger Global Management
rounds.robotnik_take: First close of a Series H at $7.6B post-money funds the US suburban rollout (Houston, Phoenix, Seattle) — the actual test of whether Zipline's economics work outside subsidized health-care delivery. Crossover-heavy syndicate (Fidelity, Baillie Gifford, Tiger, Valor) reads as IPO prep; closest public proxy is no one in autonomous delivery, with Wing (GOOGL subsidiary) and Matternet as private comps. Read this as the cleanest test of whether autonomous logistics scales without being acquired.
rounds.company_description: Operates an autonomous drone delivery network for medical supplies, retail goods, and food. Started with blood and vaccine delivery in Rwanda and Ghana; now expanding US operations to Houston, Phoenix, and Seattle. Builds both the fixed-wing delivery drones and the operating software stack.

rounds.co_investors: M12 (Microsoft), Carbon Direct Capital, Aramco Ventures, Bosch Ventures, Tectonic Ventures, Space Capital
rounds.robotnik_take: M12 (Microsoft) alongside Gates Frontier, Bosch Ventures, and Aramco Ventures is the load-bearing strategic signal — hyperscaler + diversified-strategic backing positions Neurophos as the most-validated alt-photonic architecture in the dataset. Comp set: Lightmatter ($4.4B), Celestial AI ($2.5B), Olix Computing ($1B), Q.ANT (Germany) on the photonic-inference side. The metasurface modulator approach is genuinely novel vs the Mach-Zehnder dominant architecture. Capital base ($118M total) is light for photonic-foundry economics.
rounds.company_description: Builds metasurface-based optical AI inference chips spun out of Duke University. Uses metamaterial modulators much smaller than standard photonic foundry cells; competes with Lightmatter and Celestial AI in photonic compute.

rounds.co_investors: Canada Growth Fund, additional existing investors
rounds.robotnik_take: T. Rowe Price leading a rare-earth-recycling Series C alongside Canada Growth Fund signals institutional capital is now treating REE recycling as a real industrial category, not an ESG-flavored thought experiment. Comp set: MP Materials (MP) on integrated mining + processing, Energy Fuels (UUUU), USA Rare Earth (USAR), Lynas (LYC AU) on primary processing; Noveon Magnetics and Phoenix Tailings on the recycling side. Chinese export-control overhang on REE magnets makes recycled feedstock structurally valuable to Western OEMs.
rounds.company_description: Recycles rare-earth permanent magnets from end-of-life EV motors, wind turbines, and hard drives using its Mag-Cycle process. Operates Hub100, a first commercial demonstration facility, as a circular alternative to primary rare earth mining.

rounds.co_investors: China Life Private Equity, Pudong Venture Capital, Xuhui Capital, Wuxi Liangxi Fund, Xiamen ITG Group, Huaqin Technology, Tencent, Qiming Venture Partners, 5Y Capital
rounds.robotnik_take: State-fund-led round at 718M makes StepFun the most explicitly Shanghai-backed of the Chinese foundation model champions — distinguishes it from Moonshot (Alibaba/Tencent anchored) and DeepSeek (private). Comp framing: Moonshot AI, Zhipu, MiniMax, and Baidu (BIDU) in domestic LLMs; embodied-AI extensions a likely next pivot given multimodal focus. Less interesting as a pure LLM bet than as evidence Shanghai is building its own state-aligned AI champion outside Beijing's orbit.
rounds.company_description: Chinese AI lab developing large language and multimodal foundation models. Backed by Shanghai SDIC, a state-aligned investor; competes with Moonshot AI, ByteDance, and Baidu in the Chinese LLM market.

rounds.co_investors: NVentures (NVIDIA), DST Global, Felicis Ventures
rounds.robotnik_take: Series A at 4B for pre-commercial EDA — founder pedigree (DeepMind AlphaChip creators) is the entire thesis. Comp set: Synopsys (SNPS) and Cadence (CDNS) on the public-EDA side; Ricursive is positioned as the AI-native disruptor to both. The recursive self-improvement framing (AI designs silicon for next-gen AI) is fundable narrative but unproven; real test is design wins at hyperscalers building custom AI silicon. NVIDIA (via NVentures), DST, and Lightspeed lineup is conviction-stacked but reflects narrative more than commercial pull.
rounds.company_description: Builds an AI-driven semiconductor design platform that uses machine learning to generate chip layouts. Founded by the creators of Google DeepMind's AlphaChip, targeting EDA tooling and custom-silicon design services.

rounds.robotnik_take: Software-defined phased-array ground stations + $49.8M Space Force contract in parallel is the cleanest dual-validation in the satcom-ground segment — Northwood is being underwritten on DoD pull, not commercial constellation revenue. Comp set: KSAT, Viasat (VSAT), and Comtech (CMTL) on legacy ground stations; AWS Ground Station and Azure Orbital as hyperscaler counter; ATLAS and Leaf Space as private peers. Ground infrastructure is the unsexy bottleneck for the 10,000-satellite era, and DoD prefers single-vendor stack delivery.
rounds.company_description: Builds software-defined ground stations for satellite communications, replacing dish-by-dish fixed infrastructure with a phased-array, multi-mission antenna platform. Targets defense and commercial constellation operators.

rounds.robotnik_take: German SME-cobot platform raising at growth scale despite legacy industrial robotics being mid-cycle weak — the bet is on plug-and-play modularity collapsing the SME integration cost that has been the binding constraint since Universal Robots scaled. Comp set: Universal Robots (Teradyne TER), FANUC (6954 JP), ABB (ABBN SW), Kawasaki on industrial robots; Vention and Mech-Mind on modular configurator software. Lightspeed + Lingotto (Agnelli) co-leading hints at Stellantis/CNH/Iveco distribution pull.
rounds.company_description: German plug-and-play modular collaborative robot kits aimed at small and medium-sized manufacturers. Sells configurable robot cells with low integration overhead; expanding US presence with operations in San Francisco and Austin.

rounds.co_investors: Uber, NVentures (NVIDIA), Volvo Group Venture Capital, Porsche Automobil Holding, BlackRock, Radical Ventures, ADIA subsidiary, HarbourVest Partners, Incharge Capital
rounds.robotnik_take: Pivot from autonomous trucking alone to robotaxi expansion — competitive overlap with Waymo and Wayve widens. The simulation-first training approach differentiates Waabi from heavy-fleet competitors (Aurora AUR), but at 750M Series C Waabi is now committed to scale, not just R&D. Uber's $250M milestone-based check is the interesting structure: it's commitment-without-conviction and signals Uber is hedging across multiple AV partners (also a Waymo and Wayve investor).
rounds.company_description: Develops AI-powered autonomous driving software for Class 8 freight trucks and robotaxis. Uses a simulation-first generative AI approach for training and validation, distinct from heavy-real-world-fleet competitors. Founded by Uber ATG's former chief scientist.

rounds.robotnik_take: Series B extension with sole-lead Cogito Capital is conspicuously thin for a pick-and-place specialist three years after the original Series B — runway-extension framing reads as bridge financing rather than growth round. Comp set: Covariant on US AI-pick peers (acquired by Amazon in 2024), Sereact on EU peer, RightHand Robotics on US private, Symbotic (SYM) on listed-warehouse counter, AutoStore (AUTO NO) on goods-to-person. E-commerce automation TAM is real; Nomagic's positioning is squeezed between hyperscaler-backed Covariant successor and EU sovereign peers.
rounds.company_description: Polish warehouse robotics company specializing in pick-and-place automation for e-commerce fulfillment. Competes with RightHand Robotics, Covariant, and Berkshire Grey.

rounds.co_investors: Liquid Capital, Leland Ventures, Covey, LD Capital, M77 Ventures, Block Maven, Framework Ventures
rounds.robotnik_take: Robotics-DePIN intersection is a narrow but distinct category — Konnex sits between physical-AI infrastructure and tokenized labor markets, with Framework Ventures crossover signaling crypto-native conviction. Comp set: Auki Labs on spatial-AI DePIN, GeodNet on RTK-GNSS DePIN, Helium-IOT (Helium Foundation) on hotspot peer; Hivemapper on mapping DePIN. KNX token economics depend on robot-fleet onboarding, the binary risk. Modest by tokenized AI/DePIN standards — Bittensor and Render comparables clear at much higher capitalization.
rounds.company_description: Blockchain platform decentralizing autonomous robotic labor markets via smart contracts and KNX tokens. Targets DePIN-style coordination of autonomous robots; positioned in the robotics-DePIN intersection alongside Auki Labs and GeodNet.

rounds.lead_investors: Dragoneer Investment Group, DST Global, Sequoia Capital
rounds.co_investors: Andreessen Horowitz, Mubadala Capital, Bessemer Venture Partners, Silver Lake, Tiger Global Management, T. Rowe Price, BDT & MSD Partners, CapitalG, Fidelity Management & Research, GV, Kleiner Perkins, Perry Creek Capital, Temasek
rounds.robotnik_take: Largest single AV raise ever; $126B post-money puts Waymo above most public auto OEMs and resets the bar for what a robotaxi unicorn is worth. Comp set: Tesla (TSLA) FSD as the only credible domestic rival; Baidu Apollo and Pony.ai (PONY) in China; Wayve and Waabi as private-market peers a tier below. Crossover-heavy syndicate (Sequoia, Dragoneer, Fidelity, T. Rowe) reads as IPO conditioning more than growth capital.
rounds.company_description: Develops autonomous driving technology and operates commercial robotaxi services in multiple U.S. cities. Subsidiary of Alphabet; runs a Level 4 driverless ride-hail business under the Waymo One brand using a sensor-rich vehicle platform with custom lidar, radar, and cameras.

rounds.co_investors: Benchmark, Fidelity Management & Research, AMD, Coatue, Atreides Management, Alpha Wave Global, Altimeter Capital, 1789 Capital
rounds.robotnik_take: Pre-IPO mark at $23B sets the floor for the April S-1 at $22-25B — Tiger leading with AMD strategic alongside is the clearest signal Cerebras is preparing public listing inside two months. AMD's participation is the interesting tell: an architectural competitor putting capital in suggests AMD reads wafer-scale as complementary to its MI accelerator roadmap rather than substitutionary. Read this and the April filing as one event.
rounds.company_description: Designs wafer-scale AI processors and the systems that ship around them, including the CS-3 supercomputer and on-premises and cloud inference offerings. The wafer-scale approach packages an entire silicon wafer into a single chip with 900,000+ cores, targeting large-model training and inference workloads.

rounds.lead_investors: ARENA Private Wealth, Jump Trading, Unless
rounds.co_investors: Qatar Investment Authority, Arm Holdings, Helena, Valor Equity Partners, Atreides Management, DFJ Growth, Resilience Reserve, Flume Ventures, 1517
rounds.robotnik_take: Memory-bound architecture bet on AI inference economics — Positron's claim is <1/3 the power of NVIDIA H100 at comparable throughput. Comp set: Cerebras (wafer-scale), Groq (LPU), Tenstorrent, SambaNova on architectural alternatives; NVIDIA (NVDA) as the franchise to dislodge. Arm Holdings (ARM) on the cap table is the strategic tell — ARM positioning Positron as a chiplet partner for ARM-native inference servers. At 1B valuation, Positron is priced as a credible inference-share play but with substantially less validation than Cerebras or Groq.
rounds.company_description: Designs the Atlas memory-centric AI inference chip, architected around high-bandwidth memory to run large language models at lower power than GPU-based inference. Competes with NVIDIA H100/B200 in AI inference workloads.

rounds.co_investors: Xora, 8VC, Eclipse Ventures, Emergence Capital, Perry Creek Capital, NVentures (NVIDIA), Tishman Speyer, MIT, Georgian, Incharge Capital, C4 Ventures
rounds.robotnik_take: Retrofit-kit-on-existing-fleet model is the structurally smartest go-to-market in heavy-equipment autonomy — Bedrock avoids the OEM-displacement battle and rides Komatsu (6301 JP), Caterpillar (CAT), Hitachi (6305 JP) installed base. Comp set: Built Robotics (private, similar retrofit model), Caterpillar's own Cat MineStar, Hitachi (6305 JP), Komatsu autonomous truck programs. Ex-Waymo founding team carries an autonomy IP and recruiting moat. The 1.75B post-money is rich for a Series B but defensible if the retrofit kit ships in 2027 at promised cost basis.
rounds.company_description: Builds the Bedrock Operator, a retrofit autonomy kit that converts 20-80 ton excavators into autonomous earth-moving machines. Founded by former Waymo engineers; sells to construction and earthworks contractors.

rounds.robotnik_take: Extension on the Oct-25 Series D brings cumulative raise to 1.34B — Stoke is now the second-best-funded fully-reusable launch program globally after SpaceX. Comp set is narrow: Rocket Lab (RKLB) on the commercial side, Blue Origin private, Relativity privately. NSSL Phase 3 Lane 1 award is the binary catalyst; without it, capital efficiency math breaks. First Nova flight test is the critical de-risk; existing capital base now buys ~3 years of runway through that milestone.
rounds.company_description: Develops Nova, a fully reusable two-stage medium-lift rocket. Both stages are designed to return and land for refurbishment. Targets US national security launch contracts (NSSL Phase 3 Lane 1) alongside commercial customers.

rounds.co_investors: Plural, Vertex Ventures, LocalGlobe, Entrepreneurs First
rounds.robotnik_take: UK photonic-inference unicorn at $1B — the round is more about staking out a European photonic-AI champion than near-term revenue. Comp set on inference-photonics: Lightmatter, Celestial AI, Q.ANT (Germany); Ayar Labs sits adjacent on interconnect. Strategic frame is sovereignty: Olix is the closest thing the UK has to a credible non-NVIDIA (NVDA) inference silicon bet, which is the only reason an undisclosed-lead $220M Series A clears. Valuation looks stretched without a foundry partner disclosure.
rounds.company_description: Develops the OTPU, a photonic AI inference chip targeting low-power, low-latency edge and data center deployments. UK-based; first products planned for 2027 shipment.

rounds.co_investors: AT&T Ventures, John Deere, Qatar Investment Authority, PEAK6
rounds.robotnik_take: Mercedes-Benz on the cap table alongside Google and B Capital is the load-bearing fact — automotive OEM pull is the closest thing to commercial validation in humanoid right now. Comp set: Figure AI (2.6B+ private), Agility Robotics (BMW partnership), Tesla (TSLA) Optimus, 1X. At 5.5B post, Apptronik is in the second tier behind Figure but the Mercedes pilot makes it the highest-conviction Western humanoid bet for industrial deployment specifically. Series A extension at this size is unusual — implies Series B was a structural step Apptronik wanted to skip.
rounds.company_description: Builds Apollo, a general-purpose humanoid robot for warehouse and manufacturing work. Partnered with Mercedes-Benz for factory pilot deployments; targets logistics and automotive industrial customers.

rounds.co_investors: DYNE
rounds.robotnik_take: Google (GOOG) Project Loon spinout valued at $1.3B with Battery + J2 Ventures + DYNE leading — laser optical comms is the AI-cluster-of-satellites equivalent for orbital networking, and Aalyria's Spacetime software is the routing brain. Comp set: Mynaric (now under Rocket Lab RKLB), CACI International (CACI), BridgeComm on optical terminals; SpaceX Starlink's internal ISL stack as the dominant proprietary architecture. Defense and constellation operators need a non-Starlink option; DPA Title III is the demand underpin.
rounds.company_description: Operates a laser-based free-space optical communications network for satellite-to-satellite, satellite-to-ground, and terrestrial connectivity. Spun out of Google's Project Loon; sells to defense and constellation operators.

rounds.robotnik_take: Stonecourt and HarbourVest leading without a strategic anchor is the conspicuous feature — Tomorrow.io's pitch has long been enterprise + government weather analytics, but $175M Series F without an aviation or defense prime on the cap table means the constellation buildout is being financed on pure-PE conviction. Closest public comp Spire Global (SPIR) has struggled to monetize EO-derived analytics; the read-through is that weather-tech may be a single-name story rather than a category. DPA Title III tagging hints at DoD pull as the underwriting case for the constellation.
rounds.company_description: Operates a proprietary weather satellite constellation and provides hyper-local weather prediction and analytics to enterprise customers. Targets aviation, logistics, energy, and government users with AI-native forecasts.

rounds.lead_investors: Type One Ventures, Qatar Investment Authority
rounds.co_investors: 1789 Capital, 4iG, LuminArx Capital, additional investors
rounds.robotnik_take: Hybrid equity + debt structure with QIA leading is the tell — Axiom is paying a debt-cost premium because pure equity at the prior implied valuation would mark down too aggressively against the Vast and Sierra raises in the same window. QIA participation is sovereign capital pricing optionality on Saudi/UAE crewed-mission revenue. CLD Phase 2 award is the binary; without it, Axiom is at risk of becoming a spacesuit contractor rather than a station operator.
rounds.company_description: Builds commercial space station modules that will initially attach to the International Space Station and later separate as a free-flying successor station. Also develops a next-generation spacesuit for NASA's Artemis lunar program and operates private crewed missions to the ISS.

rounds.co_investors: Hone Capital, Cathay Capital, Meituan Dragonball, Capital Today, Beijing Automotive Group, InnoVen Capital, Loyal Valley Capital
rounds.robotnik_take: Galaxea is Beijing's answer to Skild AI/Physical Intelligence — same VLA foundation-model thesis, $1.4B places it in the same Chinese humanoid second tier as AI2 Robotics. Comp set: Skild ($14B Western lead), Physical Intelligence ($11B), Rhoda AI ($1.7B) on the brain-licensing side; Unitree, Galbot, AI2 Robotics on the hardware side. Jinding Capital lead alongside Meituan Dragonball, Beijing Automotive, and InnoVen is a strategic-heavy cap table. Chinese embodied-AI software is bifurcating from hardware OEMs the same way it has in the US.
rounds.company_description: Chinese humanoid robot company developing general-purpose embodied AI platforms for industrial and commercial applications. Competes with Galbot, Unitree, and Agibot in the Chinese humanoid market.

rounds.co_investors: Spring Partners, Chengdu Industry Group, Qianlima Capital
rounds.robotnik_take: Largest Chinese commercial launch raise on record; the entity name confusion (Chinese iSpace vs Japanese ispace 9348) matters less than the signal — Chinese state-aligned capital is funding reusable launch infrastructure as a sovereign capability. Closest public comps: Rocket Lab (RKLB) globally and Tokyo-listed 9348 in cislunar. The China launch race is a 5-name field (LandSpace, Galactic Energy, iSpace, Space Pioneer, Deep Blue Aerospace); this round consolidates iSpace as the top private. Export-control insulation is the structural moat.
rounds.company_description: Japanese lunar exploration company developing the HAKUTO-R lunar lander and Series 3 lander for cislunar cargo missions. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (9348). Not to be confused with the Chinese launch company iSpace / Beijing Interstellar Glory.

rounds.co_investors: 8VC, Doepfner Capital, In-Q-Tel, NATO Innovation Fund
rounds.robotnik_take: $1.2B unicorn mark on the back of a Eur2.4B Bundeswehr framework contract is government-pull at the cleanest extreme — Stark is being priced like a defense-prime in formation, not a venture-stage drone startup. Comp set: Helsing on AI-defense software, Anduril on US defense-tech, Quantum Systems (Florian Seibel's prior) on EU ISR drones, Tekever on Portuguese ISR, Shield AI on US autonomy; Rheinmetall (RHM GR) and Hensoldt (HAG GR) as the listed European defense-prime counterparts. Lithuania deployment is the binary execution gate.
rounds.company_description: German developer of weaponized drone systems for armed forces. Holds a Eur2.4B framework agreement with the German Bundeswehr, with deployment to a Lithuania-based brigade by end-2026. Founded in 2024 by Florian Seibel (formerly of Quantum Systems).

rounds.co_investors: Bessemer Venture Partners, Micron, MediaTek, Ericsson
rounds.robotnik_take: Matter Venture Partners (TSMC-backed) leading with Micron, MediaTek, and Ericsson strategic is the strongest semiconductor-customer endorsement an AI-EDA startup has received this cycle — the buyer list is essentially the cap table. Comp set: Cognichip on AI-for-chip-design, Synopsys (SNPS) DSO.ai and Cadence (CDNS) Cerebrus on the EDA-incumbent counter, Quilter and Silimate on private peers. AI-agent automation of verification is the cleanest near-term productivity wedge for foundries at advanced nodes.
rounds.company_description: Builds AI agents that automate semiconductor verification and design workflows. Strategic backing from TSMC-affiliated Matter Venture Partners; competes with Synopsys and Cadence on AI-enabled design tools.

rounds.lead_investors: Autodesk, AMD, NVentures (NVIDIA), Fidelity Management & Research, Emerson Collective, Sea
rounds.robotnik_take: Largest seed/early raise in spatial AI; Autodesk (200M anchor), AMD, and NVIDIA on the cap table signal this isn't a research bet — it's a tooling and simulation infrastructure play. Comp set is NVIDIA (NVDA) Omniverse and Google DeepMind's Genie work; the strategic frame is foundation-model layer for embodied AI training data, where simulation-generated 3D worlds become the bottleneck input. Fei-Fei Li brand premium is real but the 5B mark is rich pre-revenue.
rounds.company_description: Builds large 3D world models — generative AI systems that produce navigable, physically consistent 3D environments from text or image prompts. Founded by Fei-Fei Li; targets applications in design tooling, simulation, and embodied AI.

rounds.co_investors: Fidelity Management & Research, Pierre Lamond
rounds.robotnik_take: Cleanest expression of the model-specific ASIC thesis — Taalas hardwires a single model's weights directly into silicon, the most extreme architectural lock-in in the AI-chip dataset. Comp set: Etched.ai (transformer-specific ASIC), Groq and Cerebras (IPO filed) on broader alt-architecture, NVIDIA (NVDA) as the general-purpose counter. The structural bet is real: if a frontier model holds market share for 18+ months, hardwiring economics dominate GPU economics. Quiet Capital + Fidelity + Pierre Lamond is unusually deep-pocketed for an Other-stage round.
rounds.company_description: Develops model-specific AI chips (the HC1) that hardwire the weights of a specific AI model directly into silicon, manufactured at TSMC. Claims much faster inference and lower power than general-purpose GPUs for a fixed model.

rounds.co_investors: Yusys Technologies, Sentury Tire, Guotai Haitong Securities
rounds.robotnik_take: Baidu and CRRC co-leading is the load-bearing combination — Baidu brings the embodied-AI foundation-model stack (Apollo, ERNIE) and CRRC brings industrial-deployment scale at China's state-rail operator. Comp set in Chinese humanoid: Unitree (~$7B implied), Galaxea AI ($1.4B), Galbot, plus Tesla (TSLA) Optimus and Figure on the Western counter. Strategic frame is industrial-pilot pull: CRRC factory deployments give AI2 a customer the Western humanoid pure-plays lack. $1.4B places AI2 in the second tier behind Unitree.
rounds.company_description: Chinese humanoid robot company developing AI-powered general-purpose humanoid platforms, including the AlphaBot embodied-AI product. Competes with Unitree and Galbot in the Chinese humanoid market.

rounds.co_investors: BlackRock, SiteGround Capital, Bitfury, CDP Venture Capital, EIC Fund, Samsung Catalyst Fund, Invest-NL
rounds.robotnik_take: European sovereignty play in edge AI — Innovation Industries + Invest-NL + EIC Fund signal Dutch and EU industrial-policy capital underwriting an alternative to Qualcomm (QCOM), Hailo, and Intel (INTC) Movidius. BlackRock leading the financial side is the unusual element; pension-fund capital entering EU chip sovereignty is the new structural pattern post EU Chips Act. Comp framing: Hailo (Israel, private), Mythic (US, private), Qualcomm and INTC on the public side. Automotive ADAS design wins are the binary; if Stellantis/VW/Mercedes commit, Axelera clears.
rounds.company_description: Dutch fabless designer of edge AI inference chips for computer vision and LLM workloads in automotive ADAS, robotics, and industrial applications. Competes with Qualcomm, Hailo, and Intel Movidius at the edge.

rounds.co_investors: Spark Capital, Triatomic Capital, Harpoon Ventures, Andrej Karpathy, Patrick & John Collison (Stripe), Alchip, Marvell
rounds.robotnik_take: Jane Street and Leopold Aschenbrenner's Situational Awareness co-leading is the most ideologically loaded cap table in semis — high-frequency-trading capital + AGI-pilled fund underwriting a transformer ASIC bet. Comp framing: Etched.ai (similar architectural wager), Groq, Cerebras, NVIDIA (NVDA), Google (GOOGL) TPU. Alchip and Marvell as strategic investors signal a packaging/IP partnership path. Less polished story than Etched but stronger compute-customer pull narrative; the open question is tapeout execution at TSM.
rounds.company_description: Designs custom AI ASICs optimized for transformer model training and inference. Targets large language model workloads at hyperscale, competing with NVIDIA GPUs and Google TPUs at the chip layer.

rounds.co_investors: Intel Capital, Assam Ventures, Battery Ventures, Gulf Development, Mayfield Fund, Saudi First Data, Seligman Ventures, T. Rowe Price
rounds.robotnik_take: Intel Capital's 100-150M check inside this round is the most strategically interesting element — Intel (INTC) backing a competitor's full-stack AI play either signals Foundry-customer positioning or platform-hedge against NVIDIA (NVDA). Vista leading at 350M reads as a private-equity-style structure on what was previously a venture round, implying SambaNova may be heading toward a sale rather than IPO. Comp set: Cerebras, Groq, NVIDIA DGX Cloud on full-stack enterprise AI. Less of a chip company than a platform play at this stage.
rounds.company_description: Sells the SN40L AI accelerator chip and a full-stack enterprise AI platform combining hardware, models, and software. Targets enterprises deploying generative AI on-premises or in dedicated clouds, competing with NVIDIA DGX Cloud and Cerebras.

rounds.co_investors: HongShan, Synstellation Capital, TCL Capital, 360 Capital, HouXue Capital
rounds.robotnik_take: Third Chinese humanoid round exceeding 250M in Q1 alone (alongside NEURA equivalent paths and Galaxea-class brain layer) — confirms China has entered the deployment-capital phase of the humanoid cycle while the US is still in foundation-building. Comp set: Unitree, Galbot, Xpeng (XPEV) robotics, Agibot. YF Capital (Yunfeng) anchor signals Jack Ma-network capital; Chaos Investment lead suggests state-aligned secondary. At 1.4B post-money on Series A, valuation is rich; depends entirely on government procurement pull-through.
rounds.company_description: Chinese humanoid robot company developing bipedal humanoid platforms for industrial applications. Targets factory deployment pilots and government procurement; competes with Unitree, Galbot, and XPENG robotics.

rounds.lead_investors: Eclipse Ventures, Balderton Capital, SoftBank Vision Fund 2
rounds.co_investors: Microsoft, NVentures (NVIDIA), Uber, Mercedes-Benz, Nissan, Stellantis, Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan, Baillie Gifford, British Business Bank
rounds.robotnik_take: The largest European AV raise and the cleanest test of the end-to-end learned-driving thesis vs Waymo's sensor-heavy approach. OEM-heavy syndicate (Mercedes, Nissan, Stellantis, Uber) prices Wayve as Tier-1 platform licensor rather than scaled operator — a fundamentally different unit-economics path than Waymo. Closest public proxy is Mobileye (MBLY); Wayve's $8.6B private mark looks reasonable against MBLY's market cap given the foundation-model architecture premium.
rounds.company_description: Develops end-to-end embodied AI driving models that learn driving behavior from data rather than hand-coded rules. Licenses its self-driving stack to automakers and operates ride-hail pilots in the U.K., Germany, and the U.S.

rounds.robotnik_take: $29M EIB venture-debt at the InvestEU layer is non-dilutive growth capital, an unusual structure for a satellite-IoT operator — signals OQ is mature enough to support debt service, which Iridium (IRDM) and Globalstar (GSAT) only achieved post-listing. Comp set: AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) on D2C scale, Iridium and Globalstar on listed satellite-IoT incumbency, Sateliot on EU peer. 3GPP 5G NTN standard adoption is the upside catalyst; the test is whether NB-IoT volumes ramp before debt obligations bite.
rounds.company_description: Luxembourg-based satellite IoT operator delivering 5G narrowband IoT connectivity through GEO satellites. Competes with AST SpaceMobile, Globalstar, and Iridium in satellite IoT.

rounds.co_investors: Redpoint Ventures, Thrive Capital, Felicis Ventures, Abstract Ventures
rounds.robotnik_take: $150M Series B at $1B for autonomous-systems T&E is heavy capitalization for an infrastructure-layer software business — Revel is being priced as the simulation-and-validation backbone for the defense-AV stack, not as a one-off vendor. Comp set: Applied Intuition (private, ~$15B) on AV simulation broadly, Foretellix on scenario-based testing, Ansys (ANSS) on engineering simulation; NI (now under Emerson EMR) and Keysight (KEYS) on legacy T&E. The DPA Title III tagging signals real DoD demand pull. Index leading without a defense prime on the cap table is the soft spot.
rounds.company_description: Builds an AI-driven test and evaluation platform for autonomous systems, used for validation of defense and autonomous-vehicle programs. Competes with traditional T&E vendors (National Instruments, Keysight) on simulation-first workflows.

rounds.lead_investors: Alpha Funds, KDDI Green Partners Fund, Unlock Venture Partners
rounds.robotnik_take: KDDI Green Partners Fund leading is the Japanese sovereignty-and-power-arbitrage tell — orbital data centers are a sovereign-power play for grid-constrained jurisdictions, and Japan is the most acute case. Comp set: Lonestar Data Holdings on lunar data centers, Lumen Orbit on US orbital DC, Axiom on station-attached compute, Starcloud on Starship-deployed scale; Equinix (EQIX) and Iron Mountain (IRM) as terrestrial counters. $10M seed sizing implies cooling-prototype demonstration is the near-term gate, not full orbital deployment.
rounds.company_description: Builds modular cooling systems and TILES processors for space-based data centers. Targets orbital DC infrastructure alongside Lumen Orbit/Starcloud as a thesis on space compute.

rounds.lead_investors: Hefei State-owned Investment, Hefei Haiheng, IDG Capital, China Fortune-Tech Capital, Hua Capital
rounds.co_investors: Hefei State-Owned Capital, Hefei Haiheng, China Fortune-Tech Capital, Yuanhe Puhua
rounds.robotnik_take: EV-OEM-to-silicon spinout pattern mirroring Tesla's Dojo and Xpeng's (XPEV) Turing chip — Hefei state-owned anchor signals Anhui province building its own automotive-AI cluster. Comp set: Horizon Robotics (9660 HK) as the dominant domestic ADAS SoC, Black Sesame, plus Qualcomm (QCOM) and NVIDIA (NVDA) on the foreign side. The strategic frame is China-domestic substitution: every Chinese OEM ultimately wants captive silicon, mirroring Apple's M-series strategy. Nio's first-mover advantage matters less than the volume committed.
rounds.company_description: Semiconductor spinout from Chinese EV maker NIO, developing automotive AI chips for self-driving and in-cabin compute. Competes with Qualcomm in automotive SoCs and with domestic Chinese chip designers like Horizon Robotics.

rounds.co_investors: Canon, Fujitsu, NTT, SoftBank, Sony, Development Bank of Japan
