rounds.robotnik_take: Notable not for the dollar amount but for the 32-company private co-investor list — Canon, Fujitsu, NTT, SoftBank, Sony, and DBJ effectively coupling the Japanese industrial base to the foundry's survival. This is the closest the dataset gets to a national-champion equity structure; functions as commercial commitment as much as capital, mitigating the demand-side risk that has dogged Intel Foundry. Public read-through is bearish-at-the-margin for TSM and INTC if 2nm Rapidus volumes materialize on schedule.
rounds.company_description: Japan's flagship advanced semiconductor foundry, building a fab in Chitose, Hokkaido aiming for 2nm production by 2027. Technology transfer agreement with IBM; backed by Japanese government investment.

rounds.robotnik_take: Pivot from commercial-LEO-station prime to national-security space contractor — Dream Chaser is now anchor to a broader defense play rather than the franchise itself. At 8B post-money, Sierra is valued in the same band as Axiom (350M debt+equity at similar level) and Vast (500M) but with a more diversified contract book. LuminArx leading without strategic primes participating is the soft spot — the absence of LMT/NOC/RTX strategic capital is conspicuous given the pivot narrative.
rounds.company_description: Builds the Dream Chaser reusable spaceplane for cargo missions to the International Space Station, and develops satellites and orbital infrastructure including the LIFE inflatable habitat for commercial space stations. Increasingly focused on national-security space contracts.

rounds.robotnik_take: Co-packaged optics is no longer speculative — AMD, NVIDIA, Intel, MediaTek all on the cap table is the clearest signal CPO is moving from R&D to production architecture for 2027-28 AI clusters. Public-market read-through: bearish for legacy pluggable optics names (Coherent COHR, Lumentum LITE), bullish for the silicon-photonics integration story at AVGO and MRVL. At 3.75B post-money, Ayar is priced as a strategic acquisition target as much as an independent — the customer list is essentially the buyer list.
rounds.company_description: Develops co-packaged optics (CPO) — silicon photonic chiplets integrated directly with compute and switch ASICs to replace copper interconnects in AI data centers. Strategic investors include AMD, NVIDIA, Intel, and MediaTek; manufactures at TSMC and GlobalFoundries.

rounds.robotnik_take: First external round after Jed McCaleb's self-funded build — 300M equity + 200M debt, with QIA, IQT, Mitsui, Nikon signaling sovereign and strategic conviction. Comp set: Axiom Space, Sierra Space, Blue Origin Orbital Reef on the CLD competition; Vast is the most aggressive on timeline (Haven-1 launching 2026). The structural risk is that NASA CLD Phase 2 award concentration could leave the loser without ISS-transition revenue. Watch Haven-1 launch and PAM-6 mission as the binary catalysts.
rounds.company_description: Commercial space station developer building Haven-1, a single-module station launching to LEO, and Haven-2, a multi-module follow-on positioned as an ISS successor. Competing in NASA's Commercial LEO Destinations (CLD) program against Axiom Space, Sierra Space, and Blue Origin.

rounds.robotnik_take: Stablecoin issuer backing humanoid hardware is the cycle's strangest capital pairing — Tether's check alone is twice the prior largest single investment into a pure-play humanoid co. Comp set: Figure (2.6B+ private), Apptronik (5.5B post this batch), Galaxea AI (2.9B private). The German cap table is the clearest sovereignty signal in EU humanoid; matters more than the dollar amount. At ~€4B valuation, NEURA is now the European humanoid leader, full stop.
rounds.company_description: Develops humanoid and cognitive robots equipped with onboard AI software for industrial and service applications. Flagship product is the 4NE1 humanoid, a 5.9-foot bipedal robot designed to understand natural-language instructions and handle payloads up to 220 pounds.

rounds.robotnik_take: Mitsubishi Electric as strategic anchor matters more than the headline — a Japanese aerospace prime backing a Spanish small-launcher signals European sovereign-launch capacity is being plugged into Asian customer pull rather than just EU institutional demand. Closest public comp is Rocket Lab (RKLB) on small-lift cadence; ArianeGroup and Avio remain state-aligned competition in Europe. EIB tranche makes this a hybrid sovereignty-plus-strategic round. Bottleneck is MIURA 5 maiden flight execution.
rounds.company_description: Spanish launch vehicle company developing MIURA 5, a small reusable launcher for European commercial and government missions. Mitsubishi Electric is a strategic investor anchoring Asian customer access.

rounds.robotnik_take: $11M seed with undisclosed lead is conspicuously thin for a US rare-earth/critical-minerals play in the current policy window — DPA Title III and DOE awards have lifted comparable rounds materially higher, and a quiet syndicate at this size signals technology risk rather than category enthusiasm. Comp set: MP Materials (MP) on US-listed rare-earth incumbent, Lynas (LYC AU) on ASX-listed processing, Energy Fuels (UUUU) on adjacent uranium-and-REE, USA Rare Earth as private peer. Pilot-plant validation is the binary milestone.
rounds.company_description: US developer of critical mineral extraction and processing technologies. Competes with MP Materials and other rare earth processors in domestic supply-chain build-out.

rounds.robotnik_take: Largest European Series C on record at a 4x markup in six months — the European answer to the CoreWeave/Lambda neocloud trade, with the added strategic shimmer of Stargate UK/Norway. Comp set is CoreWeave (CRWV) public and Lambda private; the differentiator is sovereign-friendly siting, which is increasingly priced into UK and Nordic deployments. NVIDIA (NVDA) on the cap table is the load-bearing endorsement; valuation looks stretched if the IPO window narrows.
rounds.company_description: Operates AI-dedicated data centers and cloud GPU compute infrastructure across Europe, North America, and Asia. Vertically integrates GPU compute, networking, storage, and orchestration software for hyperscale AI training and inference customers.

rounds.co_investors: Matter Venture Partners, additional investors
rounds.robotnik_take: $200M Series A for a stealth-emerging networking-silicon startup only clears on founder pedigree — Drew Perkins and Omar Hassen have prior franchise-grade exits in optical and networking ASICs. Direct comp set: Enfabrica (private, $5B), Astera Labs (ALAB) on the public side; Broadcom (AVGO) Tomahawk and Nvidia (NVDA) Spectrum are the architectural counters. Doerr/Socratic anchoring without a hyperscaler strategic on the cap table is the soft spot — the AI-networking thesis works only if a Microsoft, Meta, or Google design win materializes in the next 18 months.
rounds.company_description: Designs high-radix networking silicon for AI data center infrastructure. Founded by ex-Broadcom and Marvell networking ASIC veterans (Drew Perkins and Omar Hassen); targets the same AI-networking problem as Enfabrica and Astera Labs from a different architectural angle.

rounds.co_investors: Temasek, Mayfield Fund, Capricorn, additional investors
rounds.robotnik_take: Stealth-to-450M Series A at 1.7B is unusually large; Khosla + Temasek + Mayfield underwriting the video-pretraining thesis as an alternative to teleoperation-data approach used by Skild AI and Physical Intelligence. Strategic frame: if internet video generalizes to robot control, the data moat that Skild/PI have been building collapses. Valuation reasonable relative to PI ($11B at), but Rhoda is a generation behind in deployment evidence. Watch first cross-embodiment benchmarks.
rounds.company_description: Develops cross-embodiment robot foundation models (FutureVision and DVA) using a video-pretraining approach — training on internet video rather than human teleoperation data. Targets robot OEMs and integrators needing generalist control models.

rounds.robotnik_take: Croatian FPV-and-goggles pivot from consumer drone-racing into NATO defense-FPV is the cleanest war-driven category transition in this window — Ukraine combat usage has validated FPV-drone economics at a scale Russian doctrine treats as transformative. Comp set: DJI on consumer FPV, Skydio on US autonomous, AeroVironment (AVAV) Switchblade on listed loitering munitions, Quantum Systems on EU dual-use. NATO procurement is the upside catalyst; lack of disclosed lead at $14M Series A is the conspicuous weakness.
rounds.company_description: Croatian manufacturer of FPV drones and smart goggles, expanding from consumer and drone-racing markets into defense FPV combat drones. Competes with DJI in consumer FPV and with emerging defense FPV vendors.

rounds.co_investors: Andreessen Horowitz, Altimeter Capital
rounds.robotnik_take: One of the largest pure-networking-silicon raises in the dataset — Lightspeed-led 500M Series B at 4.2B implies design wins already in hand. Comp set is direct and brutal: Broadcom (AVGO) Tomahawk/Jericho, Marvell (MRVL) Teralynx, NVIDIA (NVDA) Spectrum/Quantum, plus Astera Labs (ALAB) and Cisco (CSCO) Silicon One. AVGO is the franchise to beat in scale-out switching; Nexthop's bet is that hyperscaler custom-silicon trend extends to networking. Read-through is mildly bearish for AVGO networking moat if hyperscaler design wins materialize.
rounds.company_description: Designs AI networking chips for data-center interconnect, targeting the high-radix switching demands of large AI training clusters. Competes with Broadcom and Marvell merchant networking silicon and NVIDIA's in-house networking division.

rounds.robotnik_take: Rivian (RIVN) spinning out its manufacturing-automation IP as a separate venture under RJ Scaringe is the cleanest American example of EV-OEM-to-robotics adjacency, mirroring what Xpeng (XPEV) and Tesla (TSLA) have done internally. a16z and Accel co-leading at 2B Series A signals the bet is on EV manufacturing-process IP as the moat, not the robot design itself. Closest comp: Tesla Optimus (also EV-OEM-derived), Symbotic (SYM) on warehouse automation. Pre-commercial valuation is steep; depends on whether Rivian's manufacturing-process IP actually generalizes to third-party customers.
rounds.company_description: Builds industrial robots for factory automation, leveraging EV manufacturing IP from parent company Rivian. Founded by Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe as a spinout focused on AI-powered manufacturing hardware.

rounds.robotnik_take: Coatue solo-leading at $1.15B for a consumer-humanoid pre-product is unusual sizing — the household humanoid category has been almost exclusively venture-funded until now, with crossover capital staying on the industrial side. Comp set: 1X (NEO consumer humanoid), The Bot Company (Cruise-founders), Figure on the industrial-first counter-positioning. Strategic frame is the consumer-vs-industrial humanoid bifurcation: Sunday bets consumer scales faster on demand pull, Figure and Apptronik bet industrial monetizes first.
rounds.company_description: Builds household humanoid robots for consumer use, with the Memo dishwasher robot as its launch product. Competes in the emerging consumer-humanoid category alongside 1X (NEO) and The Bot Company.

rounds.co_investors: IAG Capital Partners, NVIDIA, additional existing investors
rounds.robotnik_take: NVIDIA (NVDA) participating in a silicon-photonics extension is the actual signal — even as Nvidia builds co-packaged optics in-house with Spectrum-X, it is hedging on the merchant-photonics layer through this stake. Comp set: Ayar Labs on optical I/O, Lightmatter on photonic compute, Marvell (MRVL) and Broadcom (AVGO) on CPO silicon; Coherent (COHR) and Lumentum (LITE) as merchant laser supply. Series A extension framing suggests Series B optionality, with Nvidia's stake providing the strategic underwrite.
rounds.company_description: Develops silicon photonic components — laser-based optical interconnects — for data center and telecom applications. Competes with Ayar Labs, Intel Silicon Photonics, and Cisco in integrated photonics.

rounds.robotnik_take: Sheffield porous-silicon-anode preseed at $2.5M is early-R&D capital — academic spinout stage where the load-bearing question is whether scalable nanostructure synthesis works at cell-grade tolerances. Comp set: Sila Nanotechnologies and Group14 on US silicon-anode incumbents, Nexeon on UK porous-silicon peer, OneD Battery Sciences on silicon-nanowire coating; Shin-Etsu (4063 JP) and SUMCO (3436 JP) as the upstream silicon-feedstock listed peers. Pre-commercial; binary on first cell-maker qualification.
rounds.company_description: UK Sheffield University spinout developing porous silicon anode material for next-generation lithium-ion batteries. Competes with Sila Nanotechnologies and Group14 on silicon-anode technology.

rounds.robotnik_take: Mitsubishi Electric anchoring a Japanese additive-PCB Series F is corporate strategic concentration risk — single-investor dependency at late stage usually telegraphs an acquisition path rather than independent commercial scale. Comp set: Unimicron (3037 TT) and Ibiden (4062 JP) on traditional PCB incumbents, AT&S (ATS AV) on Austrian-listed substrate, Nan Ya PCB (8046 TT) on Taiwanese peer. SustainaCircuits additive process targets the flexible-PCB segment; the underwriting case is automotive and EV-cabin electronics adoption.
rounds.company_description: Japanese printed electronics company developing the SustainaCircuits additive circuit manufacturing process for flexible PCBs. Mitsubishi Electric is a strategic investor; competes with Unimicron and Ibiden in next-generation PCB manufacturing.

rounds.robotnik_take: DOE 500M across critical-minerals processing builds the demand floor that MP Materials (MP), Energy Fuels (UUUU), USA Rare Earth (USAR), and Lynas (LYC AU) need for project finance to clear. Strategic frame: sovereignty play paralleling DPA Title III rare-earth interventions. The structural problem the grant doesn't solve is offtake — without long-term commercial pricing commitments, processing capacity tends to be mothballed when Chinese export quotas loosen. Watch individual project awards for the actual signal.

rounds.co_investors: Jerry Yang, Gary Rieschel, Carnegie Mellon University
rounds.robotnik_take: YZi Labs (formerly Binance Labs) leading an industrial-robotics Series A is the most unusual capital-source pairing in the funding window — crypto-adjacent capital entering heavy-industry automation is either prescient or premature. Comp set: FANUC (6954 JP), ABB (ABBN SW), and KUKA (under Midea) on the incumbent side; Veo Robotics and Path Robotics on the US AI-powered industrial side. Industrial robotics has been mid-cycle weak; RoboForce's heavy-manufacturing focus is narrower than typical cobot pitches.
rounds.company_description: Builds AI-powered industrial robots for heavy manufacturing applications. Sells robotic systems for high-physical-effort tasks; competes with FANUC, ABB, and Veo Robotics in the industrial-robotics segment.

rounds.co_investors: Fidelity Management & Research, Mayfield Fund, Addition, Qualcomm Ventures, Alumni Ventures
rounds.robotnik_take: $143M Series D at $1.64B marks the first time thermal-management silicon has been priced as foundational AI infrastructure rather than a consumer-electronics niche. Qualcomm Ventures alongside Mayfield and Fidelity reads as design-win-driven — AirJet is moving from mobile/laptop demos into server/datacenter thermal envelopes where dollar TAM is an order of magnitude larger. Comp set: Vertiv (VRT) on liquid cooling, JetCool and ZutaCore on direct-to-chip. Bullish for the thermal-stack trade as GPU TDPs push past 1500W.
rounds.company_description: Designs AirJet, a solid-state active-cooling chip for laptops, smartphones, and increasingly servers. Replaces conventional fans with a silent piezoelectric cooler; relevant to thermal-envelope constraints on AI GPUs and high-power SoCs.

rounds.co_investors: Chevron Technology Ventures, Asahi Kasei, additional investors
rounds.robotnik_take: Chevron Technology Ventures and Asahi Kasei strategic participation tags KEWAZO as a chemical-and-energy industrial customer play — scaffold-logistics automation has direct payback on refinery turnarounds, where labor costs are highest. Comp set: Built Robotics on US construction autonomy, Hilti Group on the EU power-tool incumbent that would acquire, Dusty Robotics on layout-printing. Material-transport on construction sites is a real revenue category — Series A extension at $16M is modest but on-thesis for industrial-services automation.
rounds.company_description: German construction robotics company building the LIFTBOT material-transport robot that automates scaffold logistics and site material delivery. Targets construction sites with high labor turnover.

rounds.robotnik_take: Amazon acquiring an ETH Zurich legged-delivery spinout post-$22M seed is a textbook acqui-tech move — terms undisclosed but the strategic read is that Amazon is internalizing last-meter stair-climbing capability rather than partnering. Comp set: Agility Robotics (Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund stake) on bipedal logistics, Boston Dynamics under Hyundai (005380 KS) on legged platforms, ANYbotics on quadruped industrial, Unitree on China-cost legged peer. Amazon (AMZN) consolidating in-house robot-fleet IP is the strategic frame.
rounds.company_description: Swiss ETH Zurich Robotic Systems Lab spinout building stair-climbing legged delivery robots for last-meter logistics. Acquired by Amazon in March 2026; formerly known as Swiss-Mile.

rounds.robotnik_take: First quadruped/humanoid pure-play to file a public listing — sets the disclosure baseline for the entire sector. Revenue CNY 1.2B with humanoids already 51.5% of mix and CNY 105M net income makes this the only profitable humanoid name globally. The STAR Market venue and post-money implied ~$7B prices Unitree at roughly 1/3 of Figure ($25B+ private rumored) and 1/2 of Apptronik — a discount that reflects venue and geopolitics rather than fundamentals. Read-through for TSLA Optimus economics is more important than for the listing itself.
rounds.company_description: Chinese manufacturer of quadruped robots (Go2, B2) and humanoid robots (H1, G1), with humanoid products accounting for over half of revenue. Filed for a Shanghai STAR Market IPO in 2026.

rounds.co_investors: SoftBank, Synopsys, Cadence Design Systems, Alchip Technologies
rounds.robotnik_take: Strategic syndicate (Synopsys, Cadence, Alchip alongside SoftBank) is the load-bearing fact — EDA majors and a leading ASIC implementation partner co-investing signals Chord signaling is being underwritten as a complement, not a competitor, to in-house SerDes IP at SNPS and CDNS. Closest pure-play comp is Alphawave Semi (Qualcomm acquisition in progress); Astera Labs (ALAB) is the public read on die-to-die and PCIe demand. Round size only clears if hyperscaler custom-silicon programs are committing to Kandou's IP for 2027-28 tapeouts.
rounds.company_description: Swiss chip company developing high-speed interconnect IP and chiplet retimers (USB4, PCIe Gen 5, die-to-die) based on its Chord signaling technology. Competes with Synopsys and Cadence in commercial interconnect IP licensing.

rounds.robotnik_take: Microsoft leading a Norwegian lithography-equipment round is anomalous and load-bearing — a hyperscaler underwriting alt-EUV patterning means Microsoft is hedging against the ASML (ASML) monopoly and TSMC (TSM) advanced-node pricing power. Comp set: ASML on EUV, Canon (7751 JP) on nanoimprint as the alternate-paradigm bet, Applied Materials (AMAT) on etch/deposition; KLA (KLAC) on inspection. 2029 pilot fab system pushes commercial relevance well into next equipment cycle — speculative but the kind of bet only a hyperscaler can fund.
rounds.company_description: Norwegian semiconductor equipment startup developing helium ion beam lithography as a next-generation patterning approach beyond EUV. Microsoft is a strategic investor; pilot fab system targeted for 2029.

rounds.lead_investors: Amadeus Capital Partners, Oxford Science Enterprises
rounds.robotnik_take: Oxford spinout at $4.8M pre-seed sits in the long-horizon task-planning software layer — Amadeus + Oxford Science Enterprises is the standard Oxford-Cambridge institutional preseed signature, not a thesis bet. Comp set: Covariant on manipulation policies (now Amazon), Physical Intelligence on foundation models for robots, Skild AI on generalist robot brains, RAI Institute on long-horizon planning; Teradyne (TER) and ABB (ABBN SW) as the listed integrators consuming the software layer. Pre-commercial; binary on first OEM design-win.
rounds.company_description: Oxford University spinout developing AI software for long-horizon robotic task planning and execution. Targets the control-software layer for physical robot deployments.

rounds.robotnik_take: Italian university spinout at Eur995K seed is preproduction R&D capital — the bet is digital-multiplexed laser inter-satellite links displacing RF crosslinks, which is technically credible but requires multiple scale-up rounds and a flight demonstration before commercial validation. Comp set: Mynaric (delisted, Rocket Lab acquisition) on US/EU optical terminals, CACI on US ISL incumbency, TESAT (Airbus) on European space-laser heritage, BridgeComm on programmable optical mesh. Italian-MoD pull is the local angle.
rounds.company_description: Italian University of Milan spinout building inter-satellite optical communications using digital multiplexing of multiple laser channels. Targets higher LEO data rates and transmission security than RF satcom incumbents.

rounds.co_investors: Galvanize, Brevan Howard, ArcTern Ventures, Celesta Capital, Drive Capital, First Spark Ventures, Micron Ventures
rounds.robotnik_take: Samsung Catalyst Fund anchoring a thermodynamic-compute round is the load-bearing signal — a memory and foundry-adjacent strategic underwriting a novel physics-based architecture means probabilistic-AI silicon is being taken seriously beyond pure-research framing. Comp set: Extropic on stochastic compute, Lightmatter and Q.ANT on alt-architecture inference photonics, Cerebras (IPO filed) on wafer-scale; NVIDIA (NVDA) and AMD as the digital-counter. Micron Ventures on the cap table makes this a HBM-adjacent strategic bet, not pure financial.
rounds.company_description: Develops thermodynamic computing chips — physics-based stochastic compute architectures that use noise and thermal dynamics to perform probabilistic AI workloads more efficiently than digital silicon.

rounds.robotnik_take: Building-services drone autonomy is one of the few drone categories with clear unit economics and recurring revenue — pressure-washing and window-cleaning are labor-shortage markets where robot displacement math actually works. Comp set: Apellix on facade-cleaning drones, BladeBUG on wind-turbine inspection, Cyberhawk on commercial inspection; ABM Industries (ABM) and Cintas (CTAS) on the listed building-services side. Series B at $20M reads as channel-buildout capital, not technology-development financing.
rounds.company_description: Builds autonomous cleaning and maintenance drones for commercial buildings — primarily window-washing and pressure-washing drones — and industrial structures. Sells to building services and facility operators.

rounds.robotnik_take: $40M seed co-led by Visionaries and Creandum is the largest European OTV seed on record — pricing PAVE at the Impulse Space ($150M Series B) trajectory before any flight heritage. Comp set: Impulse Space on US heavy kickstage, Atomos and Orbit Fab on US OTV peers, D-Orbit on Italian-listed OTV competition. Strategic frame is European sovereign in-space logistics: ESA and EU defense customers need a non-US OTV, and PAVE is best-capitalized to fill that gap. Seed sizing implies first-flight by 2028.
rounds.company_description: Swiss in-space propulsion and orbital transfer vehicle (kickstage) startup. Targets the OTV market segment alongside Impulse Space, Orbit Fab, and Atomos for last-mile satellite delivery and orbit raising.

rounds.co_investors: Craft Ventures, ICONIQ, Woven Capital, NGP Capital, Samsung Next, Hexagon
rounds.robotnik_take: Cleanest pure-play on alternative-PNT — Xona is the only well-capitalized private bet on a LEO-based GPS alternative. Strategic frame is GPS resilience: jamming and spoofing have made LEO-PNT a Tier-1 DoD priority, and the Samsung Next + Hexagon + ICONIQ + NGP cap table reads as the most strategically loaded PNT round to date. No direct public comp; Trimble (TRMB) and Hexagon (HEXAB SS) are the incumbent ecosystem players who would either license from or acquire. Reads as eventual strategic exit more than independent operator.
rounds.company_description: Builds Pulsar, a low-earth-orbit positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT) constellation designed as a higher-precision and jam-resistant alternative to GPS. Targets autonomous vehicles, defense, and critical infrastructure.

rounds.co_investors: One Investment Management, NVentures (NVIDIA), Uber, Grab, 1789 Capital
rounds.robotnik_take: $65M Series A from Altimeter — Vulcan Elements is the US rare-earth magnet manufacturing bet against MP Materials (MP) on the integrated US side and Lynas (LYC AU) plus Chinese magnet incumbents on the global stack. Durham, NC base inherits the same defense-and-EV-traction-motor thesis that drove the separate $620M Pentagon loan. NVIDIA NVentures plus Uber, Grab reads as datacenter-and-mobility customer alignment, not pure financial. Binary: production-scale magnet output qualifying for DoD primes and EV OEMs before Chinese export controls tighten further.
rounds.company_description: US-based rare-earth permanent magnet manufacturer for defense and EV motor supply chains, building production capacity in Durham, North Carolina. Received a separate $620M Pentagon loan to scale.

rounds.robotnik_take: Korean government direct investment in a merged Rebellions/FuriosaAI is the clearest example yet of the K-CHIPS Act doing what CHIPS Act has done less aggressively in the US: state capital underwriting a sovereign AI-silicon champion. Strategic frame is foundry-customer alignment — Samsung Foundry needs domestic AI-chip volume the same way Rapidus needs Fujitsu/SoftBank pull. Comp set: NVIDIA (NVDA), AMD (AMD), Tenstorrent, Groq. The merger plus government check makes Rebellions the Korean answer for a non-Western geography.
rounds.company_description: Korean fabless designer of AI inference NPUs (ATOM, REBEL) for data center and edge applications. Merged with rival FuriosaAI to consolidate Korea's AI chip industry; manufactures at Samsung Foundry.

rounds.co_investors: Blackstone ($500M preferred + $250M delayed draw), Snowpoint Ventures, InnovationX, Riot Ventures
rounds.robotnik_take: Larger and more structured than prior Series F (1.5B equity + 500M preferred + 250M delayed draw), with Aechelon tuck-in giving the autonomy stack a real simulation moat. Closest publics are Kratos (KTOS) and AeroVironment (AVAV); the truer comp is Anduril, still private but the dominant pure-play defense-AI peer. The 12.7B valuation actually trims earlier 18B+ rumours — modest mark-up in a defense-tech market that has been pricing past the next two years of contracts.
rounds.company_description: Develops Hivemind, an AI autonomy stack for military aircraft and drones that enables operation in GPS- and communications-denied environments. Products include the V-BAT vertical-takeoff UAV and Hivemind-equipped fighter jet retrofits.

rounds.co_investors: Private investors (EUR 6M), EIC grant (EUR 2.5M)
rounds.robotnik_take: EIC Accelerator anchoring at E6M equity plus E2.5M grant plus E6M private participation is the textbook EU sovereign-tech blend — non-dilutive policy capital de-risks the equity round at half the all-in cost-of-capital. Comp set: Bradford Space and Aerojet Rocketdyne on hydrazine-replacement bipropellant, ECAPS on AF-M315E green-propellant, Phase Four on small-sat propulsion. Hydrazine phase-out is the regulatory tailwind; the test is whether ESA flight-heritage qualification clears before commercial OTV demand consolidates.
rounds.company_description: Spanish developer of green satellite propulsion — high-concentration hydrogen peroxide hypergolic bipropellant systems — replacing conventional hydrazine for in-space maneuvering.

rounds.lead_investors: Export Development Canada, Canada Infrastructure Bank
rounds.robotnik_take: $120M debt from EDC + Canada Infrastructure Bank — Torngat's Strange Lake deposit is the only credible North American heavy-REE source (dysprosium, terbium) against Lynas (LYC AU) and MP Materials (MP) on the western primary-supply stack. Heavy REEs are the China-dependence chokepoint for high-temp magnets that NdPr-focused mines like MP don't address. Sovereign debt financing rather than equity reads as critical-minerals strategic infrastructure. Binary: construction completion at the Sept-Iles separation plant before Chinese export controls on dysprosium tighten further.
rounds.company_description: Develops the Strange Lake heavy rare earth deposit in northern Quebec, with a separation plant planned in Sept-Iles. Focused on dysprosium and terbium, the heavy REEs critical for high-temperature permanent magnets.

rounds.co_investors: Hood River, Cedar Pine, Hanwha Ventures, Booz Allen Hamilton
rounds.robotnik_take: NDAA-compliant FPV/cargo drone manufacturer with 100k units/yr capacity at Huntsville is among the few US-domestic answers to the Ukraine attritable-drone scale problem. Comp set: AeroVironment (AVAV) on tactical UAS, Kratos (KTOS) on broader unmanned, Skydio on the autonomy stack, Anduril on Ghost/Bolt and the verticalized prime model. Ondas Holdings leading alongside Booz Allen, Hanwha, and Hood River reads as defense-tech-pure syndicate. Programme-of-record expansion is the binary catalyst against Chinese cost-base.
rounds.company_description: Manufactures NDAA-compliant unmanned aircraft systems including the C100 cargo drone and AM-FPV combat drone. Operates a 90,000 sq ft Huntsville plant with 100,000 drones per year of capacity; sells to the US Army and allied militaries.

rounds.co_investors: Lightspeed Venture Partners, Thrive Capital, Lux Capital
rounds.robotnik_take: Valuation doubled in four months (5.6B → 11B), with 2B raised in 12 months — pricing PI as the leading Western VLA foundation-model company. Direct comp: Skild AI (14B) and Rhoda AI (1.7B) on the brain-licensing thesis; Tesla (TSLA) Optimus and Google DeepMind RT-X on the vertically integrated side. Founders Fund leading after Lux/Thrive/Lightspeed prior round reads as conviction stacking, not signaling weakness. The brain-vs-body capital split is now decisively brain-heavy.
rounds.company_description: Develops vision-language-action (VLA) foundation models that let general-purpose robots perform physical tasks from natural-language instructions. Sells the underlying control models to robot OEMs and integrators rather than building robots itself.

rounds.robotnik_take: Fastest YC unicorn ever funds the most ambitious orbital-compute bet in the dataset — Starship-deployable data centers cooled passively in vacuum only clears if Starship economics materialize at the cadence SpaceX projects. Benchmark + EQT leading at $1.1B pre-revenue is the cleanest signal orbital-compute is being treated as a real category. Comp set is thin: Lonestar on lunar data centers, Axiom on station-attached compute. Bullish read on Starship throughput; bearish on terrestrial power/cooling for AI training.
rounds.company_description: Designs data center spacecraft for deployment on SpaceX Starship — orbital compute infrastructure cooled passively in space and powered by solar arrays. Y Combinator company; targets AI training workloads where terrestrial power and cooling are constraints.

rounds.lead_investors: Point72 Ventures, Activate Capital, Shield Capital
rounds.robotnik_take: Point72 Ventures + Activate + Shield co-leading reads as a defense-tech consortium, not financial growth — Starfish is being underwritten on the Space Force Otter contract and SDA's pivot toward active proximity operations. Comp set: Astroscale (186A JP) on the Japanese public side, ClearSpace and D-Orbit on debris/servicing, Northrop's MEV on heritage GEO life-extension; True Anomaly is the closest US pure-play on offensive proximity ops. Orbital servicing has bifurcated into weak commercial life-extension and strong SDA proximity ops — Starfish is pivoting to the latter.
rounds.company_description: Develops satellite servicing and docking technology for in-orbit life extension and inspection. Otter is the flagship servicing vehicle; won a US Space Force contract for an SDA-tier mission.

rounds.co_investors: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan (board member)
rounds.robotnik_take: Lip-Bu Tan on the board is more interesting than Seligman Ventures leading — the sitting Intel CEO underwriting an AI-for-chip-design startup signals INTC is sourcing design productivity gains externally rather than building in-house. Comp set: Synopsys (SNPS) DSO.ai and Cadence (CDNS) Cerebrus on the EDA-incumbent side; Quilter, Astrus, Silimate, and ChipAgents on the AI-EDA startup side. AI-EDA is bifurcating into cycle compression (Cognichip) and agent automation (ChipAgents). $93M cumulative is light vs the EDA majors.
rounds.company_description: Develops physics-informed AI for chip design under the Artificial Chip Intelligence (ACI) platform, claiming around 75% cost reduction and 50% faster development timelines on chip projects. Competes with Synopsys and Cadence AI design tools.

rounds.lead_investors: Beijing Financial Holdings Group, ICBC Capital
rounds.co_investors: State-backed and institutional investors
rounds.robotnik_take: Beijing Financial Holdings + ICBC Capital leading a photonic-quantum round signals Beijing is hedging across qubit modalities — superconducting (SpinQ), photonic (QBoson), and ion-trap programs all being funded in parallel rather than picking a winner. Comp set: PsiQuantum (US photonic), QuEra (US neutral atoms), QuantumCTek (688027) on the public Chinese side. National Supercomputing Center Chengdu and China Mobile as named customers is unusually concrete. The pilot chip line distinguishes QBoson from research-grade peers.
rounds.company_description: Chinese photonic quantum computing company with 100-, 550-, and 1,000-qubit systems already deployed. Customers include the National Supercomputing Center Chengdu and China Mobile; building a pilot chip production line for photonic quantum components.

rounds.co_investors: Intel Capital, Korea Investment Partners, Deep33, Israel Innovation Authority
rounds.robotnik_take: Intel Capital participating in a neutral-atom quantum seed is the cleanest signal that Intel (INTC) is hedging quantum across modalities — Intel's internal silicon-spin focus paired with this neutral-atom stake plus prior IonQ-adjacent positioning means Intel wants optionality across architectures. Comp set: Atom Computing and QuEra on neutral-atom peers, IonQ (IONQ) and Quantinuum on trapped-ion, Rigetti (RGTI) and IBM (IBM) on superconducting. Weizmann/Technion founder pedigree is the underwrite at seed stage.
rounds.company_description: Israeli neutral-atom quantum computing company spun out of Weizmann Institute and Technion. Architecture designed to scale from thousands to millions of qubits using optically trapped atom arrays.

rounds.co_investors: Apollo Global Management, NVentures (NVIDIA), Point72 Turion, T. Rowe Price, Prosperity7 Ventures, Sutter Hill Ventures
rounds.robotnik_take: Final private round before the long-telegraphed RISC-V IPO; NVIDIA strategic + Atreides lead reads as IPO syndicate forming. Comp framing is brutal: ARM (ARM) at >100B market cap is the public reference, and SiFive is being priced as the RISC-V challenger but with a fraction of ARM's design-win base and zero of its mobile-monopoly economics. Strategic argument is sovereignty — Chinese, European, and US export-control-sensitive customers all need a credible non-ARM option. SiFive IPO will be the cleanest read on whether RISC-V clears as an investable category.
rounds.company_description: Provides commercial RISC-V CPU IP cores, with over 500 designs shipped and more than 10 billion cores in deployed silicon. Targets data center, AI, automotive, and embedded customers as a licensable alternative to ARM CPU IP.

rounds.co_investors: Lux Capital, Spring Tide, DCVC, Airbus Ventures, Alumni Ventures, Balerion Space Ventures, RTX Ventures, Tamarack Global, 137 Ventures, Elysium, First Principles Group, Island Green, Overmatch, Trousdale Ventures
rounds.robotnik_take: $150M Series B at Founders Fund-led pricing positions Impulse Space as the merchant in-space transportation alternative to SpaceX-captive logistics. Comp set: Astranis on small GEO, Astroscale (186A JP) on listed orbital services, D-Orbit on European peers — no listed US pure-play. RTX Ventures + Airbus Ventures + Lux on the syndicate signals defense in-space mobility is the load-bearing customer thesis. Mueller's SpaceX propulsion lineage is the technical moat; Helios Mars-class kickstage is the binary differentiator vs incumbent rideshare buses.
rounds.company_description: Builds in-space transportation vehicles — the Mira orbital tug for last-mile satellite delivery and Helios kick stage for direct-to-GEO transfers. Founded by former SpaceX propulsion lead Tom Mueller; targets commercial and national security in-space mobility.

rounds.co_investors: Seraphim Space, AE Industrial Partners, Promus Ventures
rounds.robotnik_take: Defense-led round (formerly Isotropic Systems) to commercialise multi-orbit user terminals; reflects continued Pentagon appetite for resilient, multi-constellation comms hardware.
rounds.company_description: Formerly Isotropic Systems. UK developer of multi-orbit user terminals — phased-array antennas that simultaneously track multiple satellites across LEO, MEO, and GEO orbits. Sells primarily to defense and government communications customers.

rounds.co_investors: French Tech Seed (managed by Bpifrance)
rounds.robotnik_take: Heavily state-supported VLEO 5G NTN play; positions French sovereignty narrative against Starlink/Kuiper, but commercial proof points are years away.
rounds.company_description: French very-low-earth-orbit 5G non-terrestrial-network broadband startup. State-supported play targeting European sovereignty in direct-to-cell connectivity against Starlink and Kuiper. Later rebranded Univity.

rounds.lead_investors: Korys, European Circular Bioeconomy Fund (ECBF), Bayern Kapital
rounds.robotnik_take: Thermal-IR EO constellation focused on wildfire detection; strategically positioned at the intersection of climate-tech and EO budgets, both attracting cross-over capital.
rounds.company_description: German operator of a thermal-infrared earth observation constellation focused on wildfire detection. Sells data and analytics to forestry agencies, insurers, and emergency management organizations.

rounds.co_investors: Fuse.VC, Soma Capital, scout funds from Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia
rounds.robotnik_take: Highly oversubscribed YC seed (200+ VCs reportedly bid) for in-space data centres; thesis depends on launch costs collapsing and is unproven, but rounds like this seeded the 2025 'space DC' bubble. Rebranded Starcloud in 2025.
rounds.company_description: Builds in-space data centers — orbital compute spacecraft designed for deployment on next-generation heavy-lift launchers. Y Combinator company; rebranded as Starcloud in 2025.

rounds.co_investors: GiantLeap Capital, Human Element
rounds.robotnik_take: Oversubscribed Series D at >$2B closed less than two months after CEO Jason Kim's installation; sets the stage for Blue Ghost lunar success and 2025 Nasdaq IPO at ~$5.5B.
rounds.company_description: Builds the Alpha small launch vehicle, the Blue Ghost lunar lander, and an in-space transportation vehicle (Elytra). The Blue Ghost Mission 1 successfully landed on the Moon in 2025. Public on NASDAQ (FLY) after a 2025 IPO.

rounds.co_investors: Primo Capital, Karot Capital, ARIS Venture Capital, Vertech Finance
rounds.robotnik_take: French sovereign-aligned smallsat manufacturer scaling toward one-sat-per-week cadence; capital reflects Europe's policy push to backstop independent constellation supply chains.
rounds.company_description: French smallsat manufacturer scaling toward one-satellite-per-week production. Anchored by French sovereign capital; targets European policy push for independent constellation supply chains.

rounds.co_investors: Point72 Ventures, Booz Allen Ventures, Aero X Ventures, Trousdale Ventures, TRAC VC, Munich Re Ventures, Toyota Ventures, NFX, Industrious Ventures
rounds.robotnik_take: Defense-led round to scale Otter satellite-servicing vehicles; brought total raised >$50M and dovetails with Starfish's Space Force Otter program contract awarded earlier in 2024.
rounds.company_description: Develops satellite servicing and docking technology for in-orbit life extension and inspection. Otter is the flagship servicing vehicle; won a US Space Force contract for an SDA-tier mission.

rounds.co_investors: Bessemer Venture Partners, NGP Capital, French Tech Souveraineté, DeepTech & Climate Fonds, Bayern Kapital, EQT Ventures, Red River West, Cherry Ventures, Orbital Ventures, Omnes Real Tech Fund, Promus Ventures
rounds.robotnik_take: Largest European space Series B on record; first co-investment from French and German sovereign funds (FTS + DTCF) signals coordinated EU effort to seed an indigenous SpaceX Dragon analogue.
rounds.company_description: Develops Nyx, a reusable orbital cargo vehicle designed as a European counterpart to SpaceX Dragon, with ISS service and free-flyer missions on the roadmap. First co-investment from French and German sovereign space funds.

rounds.co_investors: M&G Catalyst, Glade Brook Capital Partners, Google, Radical Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners
rounds.robotnik_take: Series B extension to $60M ahead of the Firefly hyperspectral constellation launch in early 2025; positions Pixxel as the highest-funded hyperspectral pure-play globally and confirms institutional appetite for non-RGB EO.
rounds.company_description: Indian space company operating the Firefly hyperspectral satellite constellation. Sells hyperspectral imagery to agriculture, mining, energy, and government customers as the highest-funded hyperspectral pure-play globally.

rounds.co_investors: Solidium Oy, BlackRock, Seraphim, Plio Limited, Christo Georgiev
rounds.robotnik_take: Extension of the April 2024 round, bringing 2024 total to $158M. Sovereign Solidium and BlackRock participation underscores ICEYE's pivot from purely commercial EO to a defense-grade SAR/ISR platform with NATO-aligned demand.
rounds.company_description: Operates the world's largest commercial synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite constellation. Sells imagery and analytics to defense, intelligence, and insurance customers, with growing NATO-aligned demand for all-weather, day-and-night earth observation.

rounds.co_investors: China's National Manufacturing Transformation and Upgrading Fund, China Development Bank Science and Technology Innovation, Guosheng Capital, SIMIC Capital, Shanghai FTZ Fund
rounds.robotnik_take: State-aligned capital backing the satellite manufacturing arm of the Qianfan ('Thousand Sails') megaconstellation; clear signal that Beijing is industrialising LEO-comms supply at scale to compete with Starlink.
rounds.company_description: Chinese state-aligned satellite manufacturer supplying spacecraft to the Qianfan ('Thousand Sails') megaconstellation, a Beijing-backed LEO broadband program positioned as a Starlink competitor.

rounds.co_investors: Lockheed Martin Ventures, Kindred Ventures, Y Combinator
rounds.robotnik_take: Reentry vehicle for on-demand precision delivery from orbit. STRATFI agreement worth $71M with Space Force adds non-dilutive runway. Defense-tech reentry is becoming an investable wedge.
rounds.company_description: Builds reentry vehicles for on-demand precision delivery of cargo from orbit. Holds a $71M STRATFI agreement with the US Space Force; targets defense logistics and rapid resupply applications.

rounds.robotnik_take: On-orbit servicing and lunar robotic arms; total Series B Extension to $60.5M. NASA SBIR + DARPA orders signal traction in space-defense ecosystem. Originally Japanese, now US-based.
rounds.company_description: Builds space robotics for satellite servicing and lunar surface operations — robotic arms and rovers for in-orbit assembly and lunar exploration. Japanese-founded with US operations expanding for lunar demonstrations.

rounds.co_investors: GE Vernova, TPG Rise Climate, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Capricorn Technology Impact Fund, Coatue, Energy Impact Partners, The Engine Ventures, NGP Capital, Temasek, GIC, Prelude Ventures
rounds.robotnik_take: Iron-air long-duration storage developer using inexpensive iron metal as the active material; raise funds gigafactory ramp in West Virginia with first commercial deployments in 2025. Strategic collaboration MoU with GE Vernova accompanies the round.
rounds.company_description: Builds iron-air batteries for long-duration grid storage, using inexpensive iron as the active material to deliver 100-hour discharge at far lower cost per kWh than lithium-ion. Operating a gigafactory in Weirton, West Virginia with first commercial deployments in 2025.

rounds.co_investors: Draper Associates, First Star Ventures, Hustle Fund Angel Squad
rounds.robotnik_take: AI-driven Rapid Alloy Design (RAD) platform for engineering new alloys and composites for aerospace, automotive, mining and energy applications; positions itself as a software-led materials discovery layer rather than a producer.
rounds.company_description: Canadian AI-driven Rapid Alloy Design (RAD) platform for engineering new alloys and composites for aerospace, automotive, mining, and energy applications. Software-led materials discovery layer rather than a producer.

rounds.lead_investors: Export-Import Bank of the United States (EXIM)
rounds.robotnik_take: Non-binding letter of interest under EXIM's Make More in America program for up to $400M in debt to back a first-of-a-kind synthetic graphite anode plant; complements an earlier $117M DOE BIL grant and is structured as project debt with a minimum 10-year tenor.
rounds.company_description: Builds a first-of-a-kind synthetic graphite anode plant in Bainbridge, Georgia for US-domestic lithium-ion battery supply. Backed by a $117M DOE Bipartisan Infrastructure Law grant plus EXIM debt financing.

rounds.co_investors: In-Q-Tel, Honda Xcelerator Ventures, JGC Group
rounds.robotnik_take: Munich-based lithium-ion battery recycler using a low-acid hydrometallurgical process; In-Q-Tel and Honda anchor a strategic round to bridge to a first-of-a-kind industrial plant scaling from 9 t/day toward 30,000 t/year by 2026.
rounds.company_description: Munich-based lithium-ion battery recycler using a low-acid hydrometallurgical process. Building a first-of-a-kind plant scaling from 9 t/day toward 30,000 t/year by 2026; strategic backers include In-Q-Tel and Honda.

rounds.lead_investors: U.S. Department of Energy Loan Programs Office (ATVM)
rounds.robotnik_take: Conditional commitment for a direct ATVM loan to fund a 31,500 t/yr synthetic graphite anode plant; structured in two tranches against a $943.6M total project cost and includes $62.8M of capitalized interest. Borrower is publicly listed (ASX/NASDAQ: NVX) but the discrete loan event materially de-risks the US graphite buildout.
rounds.company_description: Manufactures synthetic graphite anode material for lithium-ion batteries, with a planned 31,500 tons/year US plant. Public on ASX and NASDAQ (NVX); supported by a conditional commitment from the DOE ATVM loan program.

rounds.co_investors: XTX Markets, Corner Capital, Protagonist Management, MESH Ventures, Export Development Canada, Healthcare of Ontario Pension Plan, LG Electronics, Hyundai Motor Group, Fidelity Management & Research, Baillie Gifford, Bezos Expeditions, Innovation Engine
rounds.robotnik_take: Largest chip-design VC round of 2024; pre-money $2B, post-money ~$2.7B. Open-source RISC-V AI accelerator strategy; Korean strategic capital (Samsung, LG, Hyundai) signals Asian hyperscalers seeking GPU alternatives.
rounds.company_description: Designs RISC-V CPUs and AI processors and licenses the underlying IP, led by chip architect Jim Keller. Strategic investors include Hyundai/Kia (for automotive silicon) and Samsung Catalyst (foundry alignment). Targets a licensable AI-IP model comparable to ARM's CPU IP playbook.

rounds.co_investors: Fidelity Management & Research, GV (Google Ventures), HPE Pathfinder
rounds.robotnik_take: Photonic compute / 3D-stacked photonics for AI interconnect; valuation 4x'd from $1.2B (Dec 2023) to $4.4B in 10 months — purest comparable for Celestial AI / Ayar Labs / Xscape benchmarking.
